ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p16/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p16/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p16/r3.claim: The apparent reading treats la as emphatic and redundant: the question asks what prevented Iblis from fulfilling prostration, matching the parallel wording without la.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p16/r3.anchor: الظاهر أن لا زائدة تفيد التوكيد والتحقيق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p16/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p16/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p16/r4.claim: Poetic examples are offered for redundant la, but Abu Hayyan rejects the first as proof because la may be a conjunction with an omitted complement.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p16/r4.anchor: وأقول لا حجة في البيت الأول إذ يحتمل أن لا تكون فيه لا زائدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p16/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p16/r5.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p16/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj construes la as the object and al-bukhl as its substitute in the second poetic example.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p16/r5.anchor: فقال الزجاج لا مفعولة والبخل بدل منها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p16/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p16/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p16/r6.claim: Abu ʿAmr reports a different vocalization: la is genitive through annexation to al-bukhl, since la can be spoken without denoting miserliness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p16/r6.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو بن العلاء: الرواية فيه لا البخل بخفض اللام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p16/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p16/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p16/r7.claim: Abu Hayyan offers another parsing of the second poem: al-bukhl is a purpose object and la is the direct object.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p16/r7.anchor: وهو أن ينتصب البخل على أنه مفعول من أجله ولا مفعولة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p16/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p16/r8.speaker: قوم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p16/r8.claim: Others deny that la is redundant, either supplying a missing phrase that makes sense of the negation or taking mana as meaning forbade or told you not to prostrate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p16/r8.anchor: وقال قوم: لا في أن لا تسجد ليست زائدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p17/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p17/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p17/r1.claim: Iblis’s answer does not directly answer the question, but implies that he considered his superior origin a reason to refuse serving Adam.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p17/r1.anchor: هذا ليس بجواب مطابق للسؤال لكنه يتضمن الجواب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p17/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p17/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p17/r2.claim: Iblis’s argument assumes fire is superior because it is bright, celestial, subtle, light, hot, and active, whereas clay is dark, dense, heavy, cold, and receptive.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p17/r2.anchor: النار جسم مشرق علوي لطيف خفيف حار يابس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p17/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p17/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p17/r3.claim: Those defending Iblis’s comparison say an origin made from the better substance should be better and should not serve an inferior, as reason would reject eminent scholars serving lesser ones.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p17/r3.anchor: فالمخلوق من الأفضل أفضل فلا يؤمر الأفضل بخدمة المفضول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p17/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p17/r4.speaker: القفال
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p17/r4.claim: Al-Qaffal argues that clay’s gravity, patience, humility, and forbearance suit Adam’s repentance and forgiveness, while fire’s volatility and elevation suit Iblis’s pride, curse, and punishment.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p17/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p17/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p17/r5.claim: The two materials are equally created inanimate matter, so the claimed premise that every fire-origin is superior to every clay-origin fails.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p17/r5.anchor: وهما في درجة واحدة من حيث هما جماد مخلوق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p17/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p17/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p17/r6.claim: Material origin does not establish the superiority of a creature’s form, since excellence is God’s gift; a believing Abyssinian is better than a Qurashi unbeliever.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p17/r6.anchor: لا يدل من كانت مادته أفضل على أنه تكون صورته أفضل إذا الفضيلة عطية من الله تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p18/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p18/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p18/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas, Hasan, and Ibn Sirin call Iblis the first to reason by analogy; Ibn Abbas says he erred and that religious opinion-based analogy associates its user with Iblis.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p18/r1.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والحسن وابن سيرين أول من قاس إبليس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p18/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p18/r2.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p18/r2.claim: They say worship of the sun and moon arose through analogical reasoning.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p18/r2.anchor: وقالا: وما عبدت الشمس والقمر إلا بالمقاييس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p18/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p18/r3.speaker: بعض العلماء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p18/r3.claim: Some scholars say Iblis’s analogy failed because he did not know that the spirit breathed into Adam was not made of clay.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p18/r3.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء: أخطأ قياسه وذهب علمه أن الروح الذي نفخ في آدم ليس من طين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p18/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p18/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p18/r4.claim: The story does not disprove analogy generally: Iblis used it where an explicit text applied, making this instance invalid, unlike cases without a text.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p18/r4.anchor: ولا حجة فيها لأنه قياس في مورد النص فهو فاسد فلا يدل على بطلان القياس حيث لا نص

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p18/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p18/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p18/r5.claim: The rebuke over disobeying God’s command indicates that an unqualified command entails obligation and immediate performance; otherwise Iblis would not merit blame then or later.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p18/r5.anchor: على أن مطلق الأمر يدل على الوجوب ويدل على الفور لذم إبليس على امتناعه من السجود في الحال

STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r9.claim: Verses 11–27 recount Adam's creation, temptation, and expulsion from the Garden.
STUDYQURAN:7:intro/r9.anchor:
the story of Adam’s creation, temptation, and exile from
the Garden.

ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r1.claim: Iblis argues that he is better than Adam, so it would be improper for him to bow to someone inferior; this is his stated reason for refusing.
ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r1.anchor: Yani daha faziletli, daha yükseğim. Böyle olanın mâdûnuna secde etmesi ise revâ değildir.

ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r2.claim: Iblis supports his superiority claim by contrasting his creation from fire with Adam's creation from clay, assuming the better material makes its creature better.
ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r2.anchor: Ateş ise çamurdan hayırlıdır, hayırlıdan halk olunan da hayırlıdır.

ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r3.claim: The prostration command was the first test that made divine command conflict with Iblis's own wishes and exposed his true nature.
ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r3.anchor: bu hepsi için bir imtihan olmuş ve bu imtihan İblis’in hissiyâtına dokunmuş

ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r4.claim: Iblis's earlier company with the angels did not mean he truly had their obedience; until this test, God's command and his own desire had not conflicted.
ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r4.anchor: vasfını hakikaten hâiz olduğu için değil, emr-i ilâhî ile emr-i nefsin te‘âruz etmediğinden

ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r5.claim: Iblis had in fact served his own pleasure rather than God, as his first response to a command against his wishes reveals.
ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r5.anchor: İblis hakikatte Allah’a değil, kendi zevkine ta‘abbüd edermiş

ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r6.claim: He joins a true premise about their materials to a false claim of superiority, concealing invalid major premises and presenting desire as a logical conclusion; this is the first example of satanic sophistry.
ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r6.anchor: sâdık olan kaziyye-i hilkatten kâzib olan أَنَا۠ خَيْرٌۭ مِّنْهُ da‘vâ-yı nefsânîsini istintâca kalkışmıştır

ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r7.claim: Satanic deception disguises refusal of good as knowledge by blending ignorance with learning, falsehood with truth, evil with good, and pride with flattery.
ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r7.anchor: hayırdan imtinâ‘ı tasvib için cehl ile ilmi, kizb ile sıdkı, şer ile hayrı

ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r8.claim: First, Iblis misjudges his role in answering the question: he argues back and accuses instead of admitting fault and apologizing.
ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r8.anchor: İtiraf ve i‘tizâr yerine itiraz ve tahtı’eye kalkışmıştır.

ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r9.claim: Second, Iblis resorts to analogy and independent reasoning where an explicit command governs, appealing to creation as a counterargument.
ELMALILI:7:11-18#2/r9.anchor: Mevrid-i nasta kıyas ve ictihâda kıyam etmiş, emr-i sarîhe karşı halkın delâletine müracaat eylemiştir.

ELMALILI:7:11-18#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:11-18#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:11-18#3/r1.claim: Although Iblis's account of their materials is true, he judges only by substance and ignores God's special honor to Adam, the spirit and form bestowed on him, and his vicegerent purpose.
ELMALILI:7:11-18#3/r1.anchor: yalnız madde ve unsura itibar etmek isteyen İblis

ELMALILI:7:11-18#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:11-18#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:11-18#3/r2.claim: The learned person's habit of narrowing attention to matter follows a path characteristic of Iblis.
ELMALILI:7:11-18#3/r2.anchor: maddeye kasr-ı nazar mesleki mesâlik-i İblistendir.

ELMALILI:7:11-18#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:11-18#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:11-18#3/r3.claim: Neither hidden premise is universally true: both creatures are equally created and subject to the Creator, and earth's qualities are more comprehensive and perfect than fire's.
ELMALILI:7:11-18#3/r3.anchor: ikinci kaziyye külliyetiyle sâdık olmadığı gibi birinci kaziyye de ıtlâkıyla doğru değildir.

ELMALILI:7:11-18#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:11-18#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:11-18#3/r4.claim: As a moral comparison, fire suggests lightness, anger, turmoil, and pride, while earth suggests dignity, patience, steadiness, gentleness, modesty, and generosity.
ELMALILI:7:11-18#3/r4.anchor: türâbın vakār ü sekîneti, sabr u mekânet ve sebâtı, hilm ü hayâ ve semâhati

ELMALILI:7:11-18#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:7:11-18#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:7:11-18#3/r5.claim: His flawed induction and self-sourced understanding keep Iblis from seeing Adam as God's chosen manifestation and himself as an accursed one.
ELMALILI:7:11-18#3/r5.anchor: ilmi Hak’tan değil nefsinden ahz etmek davasında bulunduğundan

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p12/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p12/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p12/.claim: The Adam–Satan episode explains the history of hostility between Satan and Adam's descendants and points to its cause.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p12/.anchor: It shows the history of the enmity between Adam and his progeny with Satan and his accomplices.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p12/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p12/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p12/.claim: Satan's hostility arose from jealousy after God commanded him to honor Adam; his arrogant refusal led to humiliating expulsion and fueled his anger.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p12/.anchor: The reason of Satan’s enmity with Adam (sws) and his progeny is because of his jealousy with them which arose when he was asked to honour them.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p12/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p12/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p12/.claim: Satan's animosity comes from humanity being preferred over him; he seeks respite to prove that preference wrong, and humans who support him effectively testify that God chose them wrongly.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p12/.anchor: the real animosity which Satan has with mankind is because of the latter being given preference over him.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.claim: Iblis is the title of the jinn who deceived Adam and rebelled against God by disobeying Him.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.anchor: who had deceived Adam (sws). He was from among the jinn and had become rebellious by disobeying God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.claim: Human and jinn followers of Iblis are treated as his progeny and are called Satans in the Qur'an; Satan is not an independent creation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.anchor: It for such humans and jinn that the Qur’ān uses the word “Satan.” It is not an independent creation, as has been explained in Sūrah al-Baqarah.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.claim: In this verse, adding lā after mā manaʿaka is redundant because negation is implicit, but it heightens the rebuke; the parallel in Ṣād 38:75 lacks it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.anchor: since the meaning of negation is already found in the expression

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.claim: The words ‘when I had ordered you’ show that Adam had no intrinsic entitlement to prostration; God conferred that status.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.anchor: Adam (sws) was not worthy of being prostrated before in the absolute sense. It was God Who made him so.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.claim: Prostration before Adam was in effect prostration before God, since it was performed at God's command.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p13/.anchor: prostration before him was actually prostration before God because it was done at His behest.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p14/.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p14/.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p14/.claim: Iblis's claim that he was superior because he came from fire while Adam came from clay makes lineage a Satanic basis for superiority; God's measure is obedience.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-3-surah-araf-07:p14/.anchor: the philosophy of regarding one’s lineage to be a basis of superiority is an invention of Satan

QASHANI:7:12-16/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:12-16/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:12-16/r1.claim: The imaginative faculty is formed from the finest parts of the animal spirit, which arises in the heart from vaporous humors and ascends to the brain; that spirit is the body's hottest element, hence its association with fire.
QASHANI:7:12-16/r1.anchor: خلقت القوة الوهمية من ألطف أجزاء الروح الحيوانية التي تحدث في القلب من بخارية الأخلاط ولطافتها وترتقي إلى الدماغ

QASHANI:7:12-16/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:12-16/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:12-16/r2.claim: Heat prompts ascent and self-elevation; each angelic faculty grasps the qualities and perfections below it but not those above it, including bodily and animal-spirit capacities.
QASHANI:7:12-16/r2.anchor: كل قوة ملكوتية تطلع على خواص ما تحتها دون ما فوقها وعلى الكمالات البدنية

QASHANI:7:12-16/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:7:12-16/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:7:12-16/r3.claim: The faculty's blindness to human spiritual and cardiac perfections causes its denial and refusal, while presuming to judge intelligibles and abstractions beyond its proper rank.
QASHANI:7:12-16/r3.anchor: واحتجابها عن الكمالات الإنسانية الروحانية والقلبية هو صورة إنكارها وعلة إبائها واستكبارها

BIQAI-FULL:v3p12/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p12/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p12/r1.claim: God's question to Iblīs exposes the disbelief he had concealed, so people can learn why he was expelled.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p12/r1.anchor: استخراجا لكفره الذي كان يخفيه بما يبدي من جوابه ليعلم الخلق سبب طرده

BIQAI-FULL:v3p12/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p12/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p12/r2.claim: The added negation in “why did you not prostrate?” intensifies the rebuke for refusing the commanded act.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p12/r2.anchor: لتنفيد التأكد بالدلالة على اللوم على الامتناع من الفعل والإقدام على الترك

BIQAI-FULL:v3p12/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p12/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p12/r3.claim: Iblīs claims superiority over Adam and says prostrating to one beneath him would be unfitting and contrary to wisdom.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p12/r3.anchor: فلا يليق لي السجود لمن هو دوني ولا أمري بذلك لأنه مناف للحكمة

BIQAI-FULL:v3p12/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p12/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p12/r4.claim: Iblīs's argument mistakes material origins for merit: fire destroys while clay nurtures, and existence is better than nonexistence.
BIQAI-FULL:v3p12/r4.anchor: الإيجاد خير من الإعدام بلا نزاع , والنار سبب الإعدام والمحق

BIQAI-FULL:v3p12/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v3p12/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v3p12/r5.claim: The basis of excellence is one's end, not the elements from which one began.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r1.claim: ما is interrogative for rebuke and reprimand.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r1.anchor: ما استفهام والمقصود به التوبيخ والتقريع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r2.claim: One grammatical view treats لا in ألا تسجد as extra, yielding the sense 'what prevented you from prostrating'; the cited line أبي جوده لا البخل is offered as a poetic parallel.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r2.anchor: قيل هي زائدة، والمعنى ما منعك أن تسجد وهي ك «لا» في قول الشاعر:

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r3.claim: Al-Zajjāj treats لا as an object and البخل as its apposition in the cited poem.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r3.anchor: وقال الزجاج: مفعولة والبخل بدل منها،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r4.speaker: يونس عن أبي عمرو بن العلاء
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarī transmits a reading of the poetic phrase with kasra on the lām of البخل, since لا can imply generosity when said in response to an order to withhold rights.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r4.anchor: وحكى الطبري عن يونس عن أبي عمرو بن العلاء: أن الرواية فيه لا البخل بخفض اللام لأن «لا» قد تتضمن جودا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r5.claim: A second poetic line, افعنك لا برق, is cited as another example of an extra لا.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r5.anchor: ومن الأبيات التي جاءت لا فيها زائدة قول الشاعر: [الكامل] افعنك لا برق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r6.claim: Other analyses deny that لا is extra: the phrase may mean what made you need to prostrate, or ما منعك may imply 'who ordered or told you,' making ألا تسجد natural.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r6.anchor: وقيل في الآية ليست لا زائدة، وإنما المعنى ما منعك فأحوجك أن تسجد، وقيل: لما كان ما منعك بمعنى من أمرك ومن قال لك حسن أن يقول بعدها ألا تسجد

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r7.claim: The overall syntax should posit a verb that can take the negation, such as 'what compelled, moved, or forced you?'​
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r7.anchor: أن يقدر في الكلام فعل يحسن حمل النفي عليه، كأنه قال ما أحوجك أو حملك أو اضطرك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r8.claim: Iblis does not directly answer the question; he argues that his perceived superiority (being created from fire rather than clay) prevented him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r8.anchor: وجواب إبليس اللعين ليس عما سئل عنه ولكنه جاء بكلام يتضمن الجواب والحجة عليه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports Iblis saying he would not prostrate because he was better, older, and stronger, reasoning that fire is stronger than clay.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r9.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أنه قال: لا أسجد وأنا خير منه وأكبر سنا وأقوى خلقا، يقول إن النار أقوى من الطين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r10.claim: Iblis wrongly assumed fire superior to clay; both are created inert matter, and the fire's height and lightness do not make its creation better, especially since Adam's breathed-in spirit is not clay.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r10.anchor: وظن إبليس أن النار أفضل من الطين وليس كذلك بل هي في درجة واحدة من حيث هي جماد مخلوق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r11.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r11.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says Iblis overlooked fire's agitation and lightness and clay's gravity, deliberation, endurance, and firmness.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378#2/r11.anchor: قال الطبري ذهب عليه ما في النار من الطيش والخفة والاضطراب، وفي الطين من الوقار والأناة والحمل والتثبت

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p379/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p379/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p379/r1.claim: The author questions al-Ṭabarī's comment on the qualities of fire and clay.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p379/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p379/r2.speaker: الحسن وابن سيرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p379/r2.claim: They say Iblis was the first to reason by analogy and that the sun and moon were worshiped only through analogical reasoning.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p379/r2.anchor: وروي عن الحسن وابن سيرين أنهما قالا: أول من قاس إبليس وما عبدت الشمس والقمر إلا بالمقاييس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p379/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p379/r3.speaker: الطبري
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p379/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explains their statement as condemning erroneous analogy.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p379/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p379/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p379/r4.claim: The wording does not show that al-Ḥasan and Ibn Sīrīn rejected analogy; they were warning against the Khārijite and other false analogies of their time and urging the straight course.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p379/r4.anchor: ولا دليل من لفظهما عليه ولا يتأول عليهما إنكار القياس، وإنما خرج كلامهما نهيا عما كان في زمنهما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r1.claim: Wa-yadharaka may coordinate with yufsidu: leaving Moses unrestrained would enable the corruption Pharaoh alleged and abandoning Pharaoh and his gods.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r1.anchor: ويذرك } عطف على { * يفسدوا } لأنه إذا تركهم ولم يمنعهم ، وكان ذلك مؤديا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r2.claim: Alternatively, wa-yadharaka answers the question with wāw like fāʾ; al-Ḥuṭayʾa's verse supplies the pattern.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r2.anchor: أو هو جواب للاستفهام بالواو كما يجاب بالفاء ، نحو قول الحطيئة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r3.claim: The accusative can be explained by an implicit an, asking whether Pharaoh would let Moses go and thereby leave Pharaoh and his gods.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r3.anchor: والنصب بإضمار ( أن ) تقديره : أيكون منك ترك موسى ، ويكون تركه إياك وآلهتك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r4.claim: The nominative reading coordinates with 'Do you leave Moses?' and asks whether he will leave Pharaoh and his gods; it may instead be independent or circumstantial.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r4.anchor: وقرىء : ( ويذرك وآلهتك بالرفع عطفا على أتذر موسى ، بمعنى : أتذره وأيذرك ، يعني

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r5.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r5.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads the verb in the jussive, treating it like yufsidu and comparing the reading fa-aṣṣaddaq wa-akun.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r5.anchor: وقرأ الحسن : ( ويذرك بالجزم ) ، كأنه قيل : يفسدوا ، كما قرىء : { فأصدق وأكن من

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r6.speaker: أنس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r6.claim: Anas reads wa-nadharaka with nūn and the accusative: Pharaoh's people would be diverted from his worship and abandon it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r6.anchor: ونذرك ) ، بالنون والنصب ، أي يصرفنا عن عبادتك فنذرها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r8.claim: One report says Pharaoh's people called the believers' mass conversion after the magicians' faith corruption and feared losing power.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r8.anchor: وروي : أنهم قالوا له ذلك ، لأنه وافق السحرة على الإيمان ستمائة ألف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r9.claim: Another explanation says Pharaoh made idols for his people to worship as intermediaries bringing them near him, like idolaters' claim that idols bring them near God.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r9.anchor: وقيل : صنع فرعون لقومه أصناما وأمرهم أن يعبدوها تقربا إليه كما يعبد

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r10.claim: This intermediary explanation is connected to the claim that idols bring worshippers near God, while Pharaoh calls himself the highest lord.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r10.anchor: ويقولون : ليقربونا إلى الله زلفى ، ولذلك قال : أنا ربكم الأعلى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r11.claim: Pharaoh threatens to resume killing the boys, reasserting dominance and showing that Moses' success did not weaken his rule.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r11.anchor: من قتل الأبناء ، ليعلموا أنا على ما كنا عليه من الغلبة والقهر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r12.claim: The renewed killing would also prevent the populace from thinking Moses was the foretold child destined to end Pharaoh's rule and from following him.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p134/r12.anchor: ولئلا يتوهم العامة أنه هو المولود الذي أخبر المنجمون والكهنة بذهاب ملكنا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135/r1.claim: Moses tells the Israelites this after Pharaoh threatens their sons, to calm and comfort them and promise victory.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135/r1.anchor: قال لهم ذلك حين قال فرعون : سنقتل أبناءهم فجزعوا منه وتضجروا يسكنهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135/r2.claim: He reminds them of God's promise to destroy the Copts and give Israel their land and homes.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135/r2.anchor: ويذكر لهم ما وعد الله بني إسرائيل من إهلاك القبط وتوريثهم أرضهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135/r3.claim: The sentence is a new independent statement, whereas the prior 'the chiefs said' is connected to the preceding clause.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135/r3.anchor: هي جملة مبتدأة مستأنفة . وأما { وقال الملا } ( الأعراف : 127 ) فمعطوفة على ما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135/r4.claim: The definite 'earth' may mean Egypt specifically, as in the linked verse about inheriting the earth, or earth generically, including Egypt as a member of the class.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135/r4.anchor: إن الارض لله } يجوز أن تكون اللام للعهد ويراد أرض مصر خاصة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135/r5.claim: The generic reading is illustrated by Ḍamra's line about a human being's two small organs: it means humanity in general while primarily applying to an individual.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135/r5.anchor: كما قال ضمرة : إنما المرء بأصغريه ، فأراد بالمرء الجنس ، وغرضه أن يتناوله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135/r6.claim: The good end promises a favorable outcome to the God-fearing among both Israelites and Copts, and that God's will encompasses them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135/r6.anchor: والعاقبة للمتقين } بشارة بأن الخاتمة المحمودة للمتقين منهم ومن القبط ، وأن المشيئة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135/r7.speaker: أبي وابن مسعود
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135/r7.claim: Ubayy and Ibn Masʿūd read al-ʿāqibata in the accusative, coordinated with al-arḍ.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135/r7.anchor: وقرأ : ( والعاقبة للمتقين ) بالنصب : أبي وابن مسعود ، عطفا على الأرض

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135#2/r1.claim: The Israelites refer to the killing of their sons before Moses' birth and its resumption after he was commissioned, as well as enslavement, forced labor, and punishment.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135#2/r1.anchor: يعنون قتل أبنائهم قبل مولد موسى عليه السلام إلى أن استنبئى ، وإعادته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135#2/r2.claim: Moses' statement that God may destroy their enemy openly clarifies the earlier implicit promise of Pharaoh's destruction and Israel's succession in Egypt.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135#2/r2.anchor: تصريح بما رمز إليه من البشارة قبل . وكشف عنه ، وهو إهلاك فرعون

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135#2/r3.claim: God will see their good and bad deeds, gratitude and ingratitude, and reward them accordingly.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135#2/r3.anchor: فيرى الكائن منكم من العمل حسنه وقبيحه وشكر لنعمة وكفرانها ، ليجازيكم على

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135#2/r4.speaker: عمرو بن عبيد
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135#2/r4.claim: A report tells of ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd reciting this verse when al-Manṣūr could not provide another loaf, then reminding him after he became caliph that his conduct remained to be seen.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p135#2/r4.anchor: وعن عمرو بن عبيد رحمه الله أنه دخل على المنصور قبل الخلافة

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r11.claim: Iblis defends his refusal by claiming superiority because he was made from fire and Adam from clay, which he regards as nobler.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r11.anchor: Iblīs explains his refusal to prostrate before Adam by asserting his superiority over Adam on the basis of the argument that he was created from fire

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r12.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r12.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r12.claim: Iblis’s fire-versus-clay argument recurs in 38:76 and is implicit in 15:33; his fire-origin also lends support to the view that he was a jinn.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r12.anchor: Iblīs’s claim to have been created from fire lends some support to the view that Iblīs was a jinn

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r13.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r13.speaker: Q, R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r13.claim: Fire’s luminosity, subtlety, and lightness coexist with fickleness, recklessness, restlessness, and destructiveness, traits that fit Iblis’s arrogance and downfall.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r13.anchor: Although fire may be luminous, subtle, and characterized by levity and lightness (Q, R, Ṭ), it is also associated with fickleness, recklessness, restlessness, and destructiveness

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r14.speaker: R, Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r14.claim: Clay is lowly and dark but also stable, humble, and forbearing; these qualities in Adam lead him to seek and receive forgiveness.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r14.anchor: clay or earth is base, heavy, dark, and low lying (R), but also has the properties of gravity, forbearance, humility, and stability.

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r15.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r15.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r15.claim: Clay can serve as a place of prayer, and its elements, water and earth, purify ritually; fire instead is a means of punishment in the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r15.anchor: water and earth—that serve as a means of ritual purification (see 4:43; 5:6), not fire

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r16.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r16.claim: By focusing only on material origin, Iblis overlooks Adam’s ennoblement through God’s Hands, His Spirit, and exceptional knowledge.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r16.anchor: Iblīs’s argument, based purely on the original substance from which Adam was created, makes Iblīs blind to other ways in which God had ennobled Adam

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r17.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r17.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r17.claim: Iblis uses human analogical reasoning, or qiyas, against a direct Divine command; Sunni jurisprudence counts qiyas among its four major legal sources, and logic also uses it.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r17.anchor: is one of the four major sources of law in Sunni schools of Islamic jurisprudence

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r18.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r18.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r18.claim: The Hanbali school generally opposes qiyas or uses it only rarely.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r18.anchor: although generally opposed or used only rarely in the Ḥanbalī school

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r19.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r19.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r19.claim: Some cite Iblis’s analogy as a reason to reject qiyas, especially in Jaʿfarī Shiism, with the slogan that Iblis was its first user.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r19.anchor: it is sometimes cited as a reason to discount or reject qiyās as a source of law, notably in the Jaʿfarī Shiite school

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r20.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r20.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r20.claim: The fault was using analogy to oppose or subvert God’s direct command, not analogical reasoning itself; jurists who accept qiyas subordinate it to Quran and Prophetic practice.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r20.anchor: the problem in the case of Iblīs stemmed not from his use of analogical reasoning as such

STUDYQURAN:7:11/r77.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r77.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r77.claim: Iblis argues for his disobedience and seeks reprieve for revenge, displaying pride and despair; Adam accepts guilt and hopes in Divine mercy.
STUDYQURAN:7:11/r77.anchor: Satan’s attitude is thus one of pride but also, it would seem, despair of Divine Forgiveness, whereas Adam’s is one of humility and hope in Divine Mercy.

TABATABAI:7:10-25#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#4/r1.speaker: قائلون
TABATABAI:7:10-25#4/r1.claim: An unnamed grammatical view treats لا as emphatic and extra, as in 57:29.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#4/r1.anchor: ولذلك ربما قيل إن " لا " زائدة جيئ بها للتأكيد كما في قوله لئلا يعلم أهل الكتاب ألا يقدرون على شيء من فضل الله الحديد 29

TABATABAI:7:10-25#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#4/r2.claim: He reads منع as carrying the sense of حمل or دعا: what caused or prompted Iblis not to bow.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#4/r2.anchor: والظاهر أن " منع " مضمن نظير معنى حمل أو دعا والمعنى ما حملك أو ما دعاك على أن لا تسجد مانعا لك

TABATABAI:7:10-25#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#4/r3.claim: Iblis’s first sin displays the root of every sin: self-assertion and a contest with God’s majesty; recognizing one’s dependence would lead to submission.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#4/r3.anchor: فإن جميع المعاصي ترجع بحسب التحليل إلى دعوى الإنية ومنازعة الله سبحانه في كبريائه

TABATABAI:7:10-25#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#4/r4.claim: By saying “I am better” instead of “my superiority prevented me,” Iblis foregrounds his ego and presents superiority as his settled reason for refusal.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#4/r4.anchor: لكنه أتى بقوله { أنا خير منه } ليظهر به الإنية، ويفيد الثبات والاستمرار

TABATABAI:7:10-25#4/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#4/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#4/r5.claim: His arrogance is directed against God, since he asserts an independent self before God, even as he also devalues Adam.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#4/r5.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن هذا التكبر هو التكبر على الله سبحانه دون التكبر على آدم

TABATABAI:7:10-25#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#5/r1.claim: The Qur’an confirms Iblis was a jinn created from fire, but this does not validate his claim that fire makes him better than Adam.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#5/r1.anchor: كان من الجن ففسق عن أمر ربه الكهف 50 وقال

TABATABAI:7:10-25#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#5/r2.claim: God does not endorse Iblis’s claim of superiority; the account of Adam’s appointment as vicegerent establishes Adam’s favor before the angels.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#5/r2.anchor: لكنه تعالى لم يصدقه فيما ذكره من خيريته منه فإنه تعالى وإن لم يرد عليه قوله { أنا خير منه خلقتني من نار } الخ، في هذه السورة إلا أنه بين فضل آدم عليه وعلى الملائكة في حديث الخلافة الذي ذكره في سورة البقرة للملائكة

TABATABAI:7:10-25#6/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#6/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#6/r1.claim: The bowing honored Adam for being formed and receiving God’s spirit, not for his earthly material; merit in created things follows divine care rather than their substance.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#6/r1.anchor: لمادته الأرضية التي سوي منها، وإنما دعوا إلى ذلك لما سواه ونفخ فيه من روحه الخاص به تعالى الحاملة للشرف كل الشرف

TABATABAI:7:10-25#6/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#6/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#6/r2.claim: God’s mention of creating Adam with both hands signals extraordinary attention and care, whatever interpretation is given to the two hands.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#6/r2.anchor: أنه تعالى اهتم بأمر خلقته كل الاهتمام واعتنى به كل الاعتناء حيث خلقه بكلتا يديه بأي معنى فسرنا اليدين

TABATABAI:7:10-25#6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#6/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#6/r3.claim: Iblis avoids the question of why he defied his Lord by discussing fire and clay; his self-assertion blinds him to the duty to obey.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#6/r3.anchor: فتعلق بأمر النار والطين، وأهمل أمر تكبره على ربه كما أنه في هذه السورة سئل عن سبب تكبره على ربه

TABATABAI:7:10-25#6/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#6/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#6/r4.claim: A divine command must be obeyed because it is God’s command, not only when a person judges it useful; otherwise interests displace God’s authority.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#6/r4.anchor: والواجب في امتثال أمره أن يمتثل لأنه أمره لا لأنه مشتمل على مصلحة أو جهة من جهات الخير والنفع

TABATABAI:7:10-25#7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#7/r1.claim: Iblis sinned and deserved expulsion by arrogantly refusing God’s command; his words express pride against God, while the verses focus on that rebellion.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#7/r1.anchor: أن إبليس إنما عصى واستحق الرجم بالتكبر على الله في عدم امتثال أمره

TABATABAI:7:10-25#7/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#7/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#7/r2.claim: Iblis’s contempt for Adam is secondary to his revolt against God; the Qur’an leaves his material-based argument largely unanswered because disobedience is the central issue.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#7/r2.anchor: فتلخص أن آيات القصة إنما تعتني بمسألة استعلائه على ربه، وأما استكباره على آدم وما احتج به على ذلك فذلك من المدلول عليه بالتبع

TABATABAI:7:10-25#7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#7/r3.claim: An objection says that a creative command cannot be disobeyed, since only a legislative command permits refusal.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#7/r3.anchor: فإن القابل للمعصية والمخالفة إنما هو الأمر التشريعي وأما الأمر التكويني فلا يقبل المعصية والتمرد البتة

TABATABAI:7:10-25#8/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#8/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#8/r5.claim: Iblis’s fire-versus-clay reasoning is a speculative analogy unfit for establishing truth; although commentators proposed rebuttals, the Qur’an focuses on his pride against God.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#8/r5.anchor: والذي ذكره إبليس في مقام الاحتجاج { أنا خير منه خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين } من القياس وهو استدلال ظني لا يعبأ به في سوق الحقائق

TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r1.claim: The prostration story depicts real relations among humanity, angels, and Iblis through the narrative of command, obedience, pride, expulsion, and dialogue; objections arise from neglecting its meaning.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r1.anchor: وجدتها صورة منبئة عن الروابط الواقعية التي بين النوع الإنساني والملائكة وإبليس

TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r2.claim: Some interpreters call the prostration command and tree prohibition ontological, but Tabataba’i rejects this: such commands cannot be disobeyed, while both Iblis and Adam disobeyed.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#13/r2.anchor: الأمر والنهي التكوينيين لا يقبلان التخلف والمخالفة، وقد خالف إبليس الأمر وخالف آدم النهي

TABATABAI:7:10-25#14/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#14/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#14/r1.claim: The Qur’an gives little detail about Iblis, identifying him as a jinn and reporting his origin in fire, without explaining his later state or the details of his creation.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#14/r1.anchor: كان من الجن ففسق عن أمر ربه

TABATABAI:7:10-25#18/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#18/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#18/r3.claim: After restating that Iblis is a jinn created from fire, Tabataba’i suggests that his first and last existence may differ.

TABATABAI:7:10-25#30/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#30/r1.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:10-25#30/r1.claim: The angels assumed Iblis belonged to them, although God knew he did not; pride brought out his claim that fire made him superior to Adam.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#30/r1.anchor: عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال إن الملائكة كانوا يحسبون أن إبليس منهم وكان في علم الله إنه ليس منهم

TABATABAI:7:10-25#30/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#30/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:7:10-25#30/r2.claim: The Prophet calls Iblis the first to reason about religion by his own opinion, when he ranked fire above clay.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#30/r2.anchor: عن جعفر بن محمد عن أبيه عن جده أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال

TABATABAI:7:10-25#31/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#31/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:7:10-25#31/r4.claim: The assertion that scholars unanimously held jinn and angels to be subtle airy bodies that physically change forms has no sound transmitted or rational proof; claimed consensus is not authoritative.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#31/r4.anchor: لا دليل عليه من نقل ثابت أو عقل، وأما ما ادعي من الإجماع ومآله إلى الاتفاق في الفهم فلا حجية لمحصله

TABATABAI:7:10-25#32/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:7:10-25#32/r7.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
TABATABAI:7:10-25#32/r7.claim: Al-Sadiq says Iblis was never an angel or a manager of heaven, though the angels thought he belonged to them and God knew otherwise.
TABATABAI:7:10-25#32/r7.anchor: فقال لم يكن من الملائكة وكانت الملائكة ترى أنه منها

THALABI:v4p218/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p218/r1.speaker: قال الشاعر
THALABI:v4p218/r1.claim: A poetic citation is offered for the construction أن لا, with the author glossing it as أن alone.
THALABI:v4p218/r1.anchor: ويلحينني في اللهو أن لا أحبه … وللهو داع دائب غير غافل أراد: أن أحبة.

THALABI:v4p218/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p218/r2.speaker: آخر
THALABI:v4p218/r2.claim: A second unnamed poet supplies another cited example containing أن لا in the discussion of the construction.
THALABI:v4p218/r2.anchor: وقال آخر: فما ألوم البيض أن لا تسخروا … لما رأيتي الشمط القفندرا

THALABI:v4p218/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p218/r3.speaker: آخر
THALABI:v4p218/r3.claim: The poet’s phrase أبى جوده لا البخل is glossed as أبى جوده البخل: his generosity refused stinginess.
THALABI:v4p218/r3.anchor: أبى جوده لا البخل واستعجلت به … نعم الفتى لا يمنع الجود قاتله أراد: أبى جوده البخل.

THALABI:v4p218/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p218/r4.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى ثعلب
THALABI:v4p218/r4.claim: Some disliked the form القالا and interpreted منع as saying, since speech and action can both prevent; the construction means who said to you not to prostrate?
THALABI:v4p218/r4.anchor: كان بعضهم يكره القالا، وتناول في المنع بمعنى القول، لأن القول والفعل يمنعان، وتقديره: من قال لك لا تسجد.

THALABI:v4p218/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p218/r5.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v4p218/r5.claim: Another explanation defines prevention as standing between someone and what they want, so the question asks what forced Iblis not to prostrate.
THALABI:v4p218/r5.anchor: قال بعضهم: معنى المنع الحول بين المرء وما يريد. والممنوع مضطر إلى خلاف ما منع منه

THALABI:v4p218/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p218/r6.speaker: إبليس
THALABI:v4p218/r6.claim: Iblis argues he is better than Adam because fire, from which he was created, is superior, purer, and brighter than clay.
THALABI:v4p218/r6.anchor: قال أنا خير منه لأنك خلقتني من نار والنار خير وأفضل وأصفى وأنور من الطين

THALABI:v4p218/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p218/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v4p218/r7.claim: Iblis was the first to reason by analogy and made a false analogy; those who base religion on personal analogy are paired with him.
THALABI:v4p218/r7.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أول من قاس إبليس. فأخطأ القياس فمن قاس الدين بشيء من رأيه قرنه مع إبليس.

THALABI:v4p218/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p218/r8.speaker: ابن سيرين
THALABI:v4p218/r8.claim: He likewise calls Iblis the first analogist and says sun and moon worship arose only through analogical reasoning.
THALABI:v4p218/r8.anchor: وقال ابن سيرين: أول من [قاس] إبليس، وما عبدت الشمس والقمر إلا بالمقاييس.

THALABI:v4p218/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p218/r9.speaker: الحكماء
THALABI:v4p218/r9.claim: They argue clay’s gravity, calm, dignity, patience, and modesty led Adam to repentance and guidance, while fire’s volatility and pride led Iblis to arrogance and ruin.
THALABI:v4p218/r9.anchor: أحدها: إن من جوهر الطين الرزانة والسكون والوقار والاناة والحلم والحياء والصبر، وذلك هو الداعي لآدم في السعادة

THALABI:v4p218/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p218/r10.speaker: الحكماء
THALABI:v4p218/r10.claim: A second argument is that clay gathers things together whereas fire separates them.
THALABI:v4p218/r10.anchor: والثاني: إن الطين سبب جمع الأشياء والنار سبب تفريقها.

THALABI:v4p218/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p218/r11.speaker: الحكماء
THALABI:v4p218/r11.claim: A third argument says the reported soil of Paradise is fragrant musk, while no report says Paradise contains fire or Hell contains soil.
THALABI:v4p218/r11.anchor: والثالث: إن الخبر ناطق بأن تراب الجنة مسك أذفر ولم ينطق الخبر بأن في الجنة نارا

THALABI:v4p218/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p218/r12.speaker: الحكماء
THALABI:v4p218/r12.claim: A fourth argument is that fire causes torment and is God’s punishment for His enemies, while soil does not cause torment.
THALABI:v4p218/r12.anchor: والرابع: إن النار سبب العذاب وهي عذاب الله لأعدائه وليس التراب سببا للعذاب.

THALABI:v4p220/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p220/r1.speaker: الحكماء
THALABI:v4p220/r1.claim: Their fifth argument is that clay is watered from fire, while fire itself needs a place and its place is soil.
THALABI:v4p220/r1.anchor: والخامس: إن الطين [يسقى] من النار والنار محتاجة إلى المكان ومكانها التراب.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:12-17/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:12-17/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:12-17/r1.claim: The extra la in the question is redundant: it asks what prevented Iblis from prostrating, as a rebuke.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:12-17/r1.anchor: قال ما منعك إلا تسجد } " لا " زائدة. معناها: ما منعك أن تسجد؟! وهو سؤال التوبيخ والتعنيف

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:12-17/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:12-17/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:12-17/r2.claim: Iblis says he refused because fire made him superior to Adam, who was made of clay; he abandoned the command, reasoned by analogy, and disobeyed.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:12-17/r2.anchor: منعني من السجود له أني خير منه إذ كنت ناريا، وكان طينيا، فترك الأمر وقاس، فعصى.

TAB-FULL:v10p81/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p81/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p81/r1.claim: God asks Iblis what kept him from refraining from prostration to Adam when commanded; the question concerns his disobedient refusal.
TAB-FULL:v10p81/r1.anchor: وهذا خبر من الله تعالى ذكره عن قيله لإبليس إذ عصاه فلم يسجد لآدم إذ أمره بالسجود له

TAB-FULL:v10p81/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p81/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p81/r2.claim: Iblis was blamed for disobeying God by leaving prostration, not for prostrating; Tabari explains how the wording can express that charge.
TAB-FULL:v10p81/r2.anchor: إن الملامة لم تلحق إبليس إلا على معصيته ربه بتركه السجود لآدم إذ أمره بالسجود له

TAB-FULL:v10p81/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p81/r3.speaker: بعض نحويي البصرة
TAB-FULL:v10p81/r3.claim: Some Basran grammarians take لا as extra, so the question means what prevented you from prostrating; they cite the poetic phrase أبى جوده لا البخل.
TAB-FULL:v10p81/r3.anchor: فقال بعض نحويي البصرة: معنى ذلك: ما منعك أن تسجد، و (لا) ههنا زائدة

TAB-FULL:v10p81/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p81/r4.speaker: يونس
TAB-FULL:v10p81/r4.claim: Yunus reports that Abu ʿAmr makes البخل genitive and treats لا as annexed to it, since لا can name either generosity or miserliness.
TAB-FULL:v10p81/r4.anchor: وزعم يونس أن أبا عمرو كان يجر (البخل) ، ويجعل (لا) مضافة إليه، أراد

TAB-FULL:v10p81/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p81/r5.speaker: بعض نحويي الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v10p81/r5.claim: Some Kufan grammarians also take لا as extra but say it repeats the negation for emphasis because the preceding verse says Iblis was not among the prostrators.
TAB-FULL:v10p81/r5.anchor: وقال بعض نحويي الكوفة نحو القول الذي ذكرناه عن البصريين

TAB-FULL:v10p83/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p83/r1.speaker: بعض نحويي الكوفة
TAB-FULL:v10p83/r1.claim: The Kufan explanation treats لا as a repeated negation, with the poem’s إن reinforcing the earlier ما.
TAB-FULL:v10p83/r1.anchor: ما إن رأينا مثلهن لمعشر … سود الروس فوالج وفيول

TAB-FULL:v10p83/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p83/r2.speaker: بعض نحويي البصرة
TAB-FULL:v10p83/r2.claim: Another grammarian says لا is neither extra nor a particle of connection: منع means ‘say,’ so the question is who told Iblis not to prostrate.
TAB-FULL:v10p83/r2.anchor: ولكن المنع ههنا بمعنى القول. إنما تأويل الكلام: من قال لك لا تسجد إذ أمرتك بالسجود

TAB-FULL:v10p83/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p83/r3.speaker: بعض من روى
TAB-FULL:v10p83/r3.claim: One transmitter interprets لا in the poem أبى جوده لا البخل as the word for miserliness itself.
TAB-FULL:v10p83/r3.anchor: بعض من روى: (أبى جوده لا البخل) بمعنى: كلمة البخل، لأن (لا) هي كلمة البخل

TAB-FULL:v10p83/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p83/r4.speaker: بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v10p83/r4.claim: Some explain منع as blocking a person from what he wants and thus compelling him to do the opposite, so the question asks what forced Iblis not to prostrate.
TAB-FULL:v10p83/r4.anchor: وقال بعضهم: معنى المنع: الحول بين المرء وما يريده، قال: والممنوع مضطر به إلى خلاف ما منع منه

TAB-FULL:v10p83/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p83/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p83/r5.claim: Tabari supplies an ellipsis: ‘What prevented you from prostrating and made you need not to?’ The suppressed أحوجك is understood from the statement that Iblis was not among the prostrators.
TAB-FULL:v10p83/r5.anchor: ما منعك من السجود فأحوجك أن لا تسجد؟ فترك ذكر أحوجك استغناء بمعرفة السامعين

TAB-FULL:v10p83/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p83/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p83/r6.claim: Tabari rejects treating لا as meaningless padding, since every word in the Qur’an has a sound meaning.
TAB-FULL:v10p83/r6.anchor: لما قد مضى من دلالتنا قبل على أنه غير جائز أن يكون في كتاب الله شيء لا معنى له، وأن لكل كلمة معنى صحيحا

TAB-FULL:v10p83/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p83/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p83/r7.claim: Tabari rejects taking منع as a command to leave prostration: a person able to obey or disobey is not prevented from acting, and Iblis would not obey another’s command after defying God.
TAB-FULL:v10p83/r7.anchor: فليس المعروف في الناس استعمال المنع في الأمر بترك الشيء، لأن المأمور بترك الفعل إذا كان قادرا على فعله وتركه

TAB-FULL:v10p85/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p85/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p85/r1.claim: Iblis claimed that he was better than Adam, stronger and more powerful because he was made from fire and Adam from clay.
TAB-FULL:v10p85/r1.anchor: أن المانع كان له من السجود والداعي له إلى خلافه أمر ربه في ذلك أنه أشد منه أيدا، وأقوى منه قوة، وأفضل منه فضلا

TAB-FULL:v10p85/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p85/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p85/r2.claim: Tabari says fire’s lightness, impetuosity, instability, and upward motion fed Iblis’s arrogance, while clay’s steadiness, patience, forbearance, modesty, and deliberation led Adam to repent and seek forgiveness; their outcomes followed prior divine decree.
TAB-FULL:v10p85/r2.anchor: من جوهر النار: الخفة والطيش والاضطراب والارتفاع علوا، والذي في جوهرها من ذلك هو الذي حمل الخبيث

TAB-FULL:v10p85/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p85/r3.speaker: الحسن وابن سيرين
TAB-FULL:v10p85/r3.claim: Al-Hasan and Ibn Sirin call Iblis the first to make an erroneous analogy; Ibn Sirin adds that the sun and moon were worshipped only through analogical reasoning.
TAB-FULL:v10p85/r3.anchor: الحسن وابن سيرين يقولان: «أول من قاس إبليس»

TAB-FULL:v10p85/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p85/r4.speaker: ابن سيرين
TAB-FULL:v10p85/r4.claim: Ibn Sirin says Iblis was the first to reason by analogy and that the sun and moon were worshipped only through analogies.
TAB-FULL:v10p85/r4.anchor: عن هشام، عن ابن سيرين، قال: «أول من قاس إبليس، وما عبدت الشمس والقمر إلا بالمقاييس»

TAB-FULL:v10p85/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p85/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p85/r5.claim: Iblis’s analogy ignored Adam’s honors: God created him with His hand, breathed into him of His spirit, commanded the angels to prostrate to him, taught him the names, and granted him many further distinctions.
TAB-FULL:v10p85/r5.anchor: الذي خص الله به آدم على سائر خلقه من خلقه إياه بيده، ونفخه فيه من روحه

TAB-FULL:v10p87/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p87/r1.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v10p87/r1.claim: Al-Hasan says Iblis was the first to make an analogy.
TAB-FULL:v10p87/r1.anchor: عن الحسن، قوله: {خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين} [الأعراف: 12] قال: «قاس إبليس، وهو أول من قاس»

TAB-FULL:v10p87/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p87/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v10p87/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that God ordered the angels accompanying Iblis to prostrate to Adam; all did except Iblis, who arrogantly claimed to be better, older, and stronger because fire is stronger than clay.
TAB-FULL:v10p87/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " لما خلق الله آدم قال للملائكة الذين كانوا مع إبليس

TAB-FULL:v10p87/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p87/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v10p87/r3.claim: Mujahid says that after Iblis was created from fire, his descendants were made from water.
TAB-FULL:v10p87/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج، عن مجاهد، قوله: {خلقتني من نار} [الأعراف: 12] قال: «ثم جعل ذريته من ماء»

TAB-FULL:v10p87/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v10p87/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v10p87/r4.claim: Tabari says Iblis did not directly answer what prevented him from prostrating; instead, he began boasting that he was better than Adam, indirectly revealing the reason.
TAB-FULL:v10p87/r4.anchor: لم يجب بأن الذي منعه من السجود: أنه خلقه من نار، وخلق آدم من طين، ولكنه ابتدأ خبرا عن نفسه، فيه دليل على موضع الجواب

TABRISI:7:12-13/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:12-13/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:12-13/r2.claim: Mā is nominative as the subject of the question, meaning what thing prevented you.
TABRISI:7:12-13/r2.anchor: ما في قوله ما منعك مرفوع الموضع والمعنى أي شيء منعك

TABRISI:7:12-13/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:12-13/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:12-13/r3.claim: The lā in an lā tasjud is treated as redundant, so the question means what prevented you from prostrating; laʾallā yaʿlama likewise means li-an yaʿlama.
TABRISI:7:12-13/r3.anchor: ولا ملغى ألا تسجد المعنى ما منعك أن تسجد ومثله قوله سبحانه لئلا يعلم ومعناه لأن يعلم

TABRISI:7:12-13/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:12-13/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:12-13/r4.claim: The common explanation of the cited poetic line is that the speaker’s generosity refuses stinginess.

TABRISI:7:12-13/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:12-13/r5.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
TABRISI:7:12-13/r5.claim: Abu Amr ibn al-Ala reports the line with al-bukhl in the genitive and construes lā as the thing that makes a person miserly.
TABRISI:7:12-13/r5.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو بن العلاء: الرواية أبى جوده لا البخل بالجر والمعنى أبى جوده لا التي تبخل الإنسان

TABRISI:7:12-13/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:12-13/r6.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:7:12-13/r6.claim: Al-Zajjāj offers another analysis: lā is not redundant, and accusative al-bukhl is an appositive to lā, yielding the sense that generosity refused stinginess.
TABRISI:7:12-13/r6.anchor: قال الزجاج: وروي فيه وجها آخر حسنا وهو أن يكون لا غير لغو ويكون البخل منصوبا بدلا من لا

TABRISI:7:12-13/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:12-13/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:12-13/r7.claim: Another explanation retains the negation: the question means what prompted or compelled you not to prostrate.
TABRISI:7:12-13/r7.anchor: وقد قيل إنما دخل لا في قوله إلا تسجد لأن معناه ما دعاك إلى أن لا تسجد

TABRISI:7:12-13/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:12-13/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:12-13/r8.claim: God questions Iblis after his refusal: what led or compelled you not to prostrate, or what prevented you from prostrating when commanded?
TABRISI:7:12-13/r8.anchor: ثم حكى سبحانه خطابه لإبليس حين امتنع من السجود لآدم

TABRISI:7:12-13/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:12-13/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:12-13/r9.claim: Iblis’s reply does not directly answer what prevented him; it answers who is better, but works as an implied response, like answering how one was by saying I am well.
TABRISI:7:12-13/r9.anchor: وهذا الجواب غير مطابق لأنه كان يجب أن يقول منعني كذا لأن قوله أنا خير منه جواب لمن يقول أيكما خير

TABRISI:7:12-13/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:12-13/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:7:12-13/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says Iblis was first to reason by analogy and err; whoever analogizes religion from personal opinion is paired by God with Iblis.
TABRISI:7:12-13/r10.anchor: قال ابن عباس أول من قاس إبليس فأخطأ القياس فمن قاس الدين بشيء من رأيه قرنه الله بإبليس

TABRISI:7:12-13/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:12-13/r11.speaker: ابن سيرين
TABRISI:7:12-13/r11.claim: Ibn Sirin likewise says Iblis was first to reason by analogy, and that the sun and moon were worshipped only through analogical reasoning.
TABRISI:7:12-13/r11.anchor: وقال ابن سيرين: أول من قاس إبليس وما عبدت الشمس والقمر إلا بالمقاييس

TABRISI:7:12-13/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:12-13/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:12-13/r12.claim: Iblis’s false premise was that fire is nobler than clay, so a superior should not bow to an inferior; obedience instead depends on God’s wisdom and the interests of His servants.
TABRISI:7:12-13/r12.anchor: ظن أن النار إذا كانت أشرف من الطين لم يجز أن يسجد الأشرف للأدون وهذا خطأ لأن ذلك تابع لما يعلم الله سبحانه من مصالح العباد

TABRISI:7:12-13/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:12-13/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:12-13/r13.claim: Another view argues clay is better than fire because earth offers greater benefits: it supports habitation and livelihood and produces provisions.
TABRISI:7:12-13/r13.anchor: وقد قيل أيضا إن الطين خير من النار لأنه أكثر منافع للخلق من حيث إن الأرض مستقر الخلق

TABRISI:7:12-13/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:7:12-13/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:7:12-13/r14.claim: Here goodness means abundance of practical benefit, not reward, which belongs only to morally responsible beings who are commanded, not inanimate matter.
TABRISI:7:12-13/r14.anchor: والخيرية إنما يراد بها كثرة المنافع دون كثرة الثواب لأن الثواب لا يكون إلا للمكلف المأمور دون الجماد

THALABI:v4p217#2/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v4p217#2/r11.speaker: بعضهم
THALABI:v4p217#2/r11.claim: Some grammarians treat لا as extra and إن as a connective, yielding “what kept you from prostrating to Adam”; they cite a parallel construction in 21:95.
THALABI:v4p217#2/r11.anchor: قال بعضهم: لا زائدة [وإن صلة] تقدير الكلام: ما منعك السجود لآدم، لأن المنع يتعدى إلى مفعولين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p41/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p41/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p41/r1.claim: ما is nominative as the subject of the question, meaning what prevented you from prostrating?
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p41/r1.anchor: موضع (ما (¬1)) رفع، المعنى: أي شيء منعك من السجود.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p41/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p41/r2.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p41/r2.claim: God asks Iblis the reason for refusing prostration although He knows it in order to rebuke him and expose his defiance and disobedience.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p41/r2.anchor: قال أبو بكر (¬2): (ومعنى سؤاله الله عز وجل إبليس عن علة ترك السجود وهو عالم بذلك التوبيخ له

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p41/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p41/r3.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p41/r3.claim: Abu Ishaq shares Abu Bakr's explanation that the question is a rebuke to Iblis.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p41/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p41/r4.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p41/r4.claim: Al-Farra says لا is extra for reinforcement: the meaning is what prevented you from prostrating; he compares 21:95 and 57:29.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p41/r4.anchor: قال الفراء: (المعنى: ما منعك أن تسجد وأن في هذا الموضع تصحبها (¬6) لا،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p41/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p41/r5.speaker: الكسائي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p41/r5.claim: Al-Kisa'i agrees that لا is extra in the construction.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p41/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p41/r6.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p41/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj likewise treats لا as an emphatic, dispensable particle, and cites poetry where generosity rejects stinginess.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p41/r6.anchor: قال الزجاج: فقال: (معنى {ما منعك ألا تسجد} إلغاء لا وهي مؤكدة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p41/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p41/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p41/r7.claim: Abu Amr's transmitted reading of the cited line is that Iblis's generosity refused the call to stinginess, as if answering no to a command not to give.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p41/r7.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو بن العلاء: الرواية أبي جوده لا البخل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p41/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p41/r8.speaker: يونس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p41/r8.claim: Yunus reports that Abu Amr construed البخل in the genitive, with لا annexed to it as the prohibition associated with stinginess.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p41/r8.anchor: وزعم يونس (¬2) أن أبا عمرو (¬3) كان يجر البخل ويجعل لا مضافة إليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p43/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p43/r1.speaker: أحمد بن يحيى
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p43/r1.claim: Ahmad ibn Yahya says لا is neither extra nor emphatic; the phrase means who told you not to prostrate?
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p43/r1.anchor: وحكى عن أحمد بن يحيى: (أن (لا) في هذه الآية ليست زائدة، ولا توكيدا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p43/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p43/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p43/r2.claim: Abu Bakr also attributes the non-extra interpretation of لا to al-Farra.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p43/r2.anchor: وهذا القول حكاه أبو بكر (¬3) عن الفراء.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p43/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p43/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p43/r3.claim: Iblis's wording is not a literal answer to what prevented prostration, but it conveys that his supposed superiority prevented him.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p43/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p43/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p43/r4.claim: Al-Zajjaj agrees that Iblis gives a phrase whose meaning answers the question though its wording does not.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p43/r4.anchor: فأتى بشيء في معنى الجواب ولفظه غير جواب؛ لأن قوله: {أنا خير منه}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p43/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p43/r5.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p43/r5.claim: Abu Bakr explains Iblis's claim as meaning that, in his own estimation, being made of fire made him superior to Adam and kept him from prostrating.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p43/r5.anchor: وزاد أبو بكر لهذا بيانا فقال: (أما قولة إبليس لعنه الله في جواب ربه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p43/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p43/r6.speaker: أبو بكر
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p43/r6.claim: Abu Bakr says Arabic permits a concise response that conveys the answer by implication, illustrated by asking whose house it is and replying that its owner is Zayd.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p43/r6.anchor: كما يقول الرجل للرجل: لمن الدار؟ فيقول: مالكها زيد، يريد هي لزيد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p43/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p43/r7.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p43/r7.claim: Abu Ishaq offers another parsing of the poem: لا is not redundant and البخل is an accusative substitute for it, meaning generosity refused stinginess.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p43/r7.anchor: أبو إسحاق في البيت قولا آخر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p45/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p45/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p45/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says obedience should have taken precedence over Iblis's analogy; Iblis was the first to reason by analogy and disbelieved through it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p45/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (كانت الطاعة أولى بإبليس من القياس،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p45/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p45/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p45/r2.claim: Analogy that opposes revealed text is rejected like Iblis's, while analogy based on established principles where no text exists is accepted by scholars.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p45/r2.anchor: قيل: القياس قياسان: قياس في مخالفة النص فهو مردود كقياس إبليس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p45/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p45/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p45/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas's warning is against judging religion by personal opinion, not against every principled scholarly analogy.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p45/r3.anchor: وابن عباس يقول: (من قاس الدين بشيء من رأيه) ولا يجوز أن يقاس الدين بما يراه الإنسان

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:12/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:12/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:12/r1.claim: God’s asking Iblis why he disobeyed without immediately expelling him recognizes the right of defense for everyone.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:12/r1.anchor: Yüce Allah’ın, İblîs’i hemen rahmetinden kovmayıp isyan etmesinin sebebini sorması, savunmayı herkes için bir hak olarak tanıdığını gösterir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:12/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:12/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:12/r2.claim: Iblis argues that fire makes him more valuable than Adam, who was made from earth; this reasoning is wrong in many respects and does not justify disobedience.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:12/r2.anchor: İblîs, kendisinin ateşten, Âdem’in ise topraktan yaratıldığı, şu halde kendisinin ondan daha değerli olduğu şeklinde bir istidlâlde bulunmuşsa da

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:12/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:12/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:12/r3.claim: Iblis was expelled from his station because of his unjustified rebellion, with special emphasis on his arrogance and resulting abasement.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:7:12/r3.anchor: Burada İblîs’in kibre kapıldığına ve bunun cezası olarak aşağılıklardan biri haline getirildiğine bilhassa dikkat çekilmektedir.

QUSHAYRI:v1p325/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p325/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p325/r1.claim: Satan’s claim of superiority should have yielded to humility, especially because the command came from the Real.
QUSHAYRI:v1p325/r1.anchor: ادعى الخيرية ، وكان الواجب عليه - لولا الشقوة - أن يؤثر التذلل على التكبر

QUSHAYRI:v1p325/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p325/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p325/r2.claim: Satan’s self-interested analogy only increased his culpability: superiority rests on God’s judgment and allotment, not on the material from which one was made.
QUSHAYRI:v1p325/r2.anchor: ولم يعلم أن الخيرية بحكمه - سبحانه - وقسمته

QUSHAYRI:v1p325/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p325/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p325/r4.claim: Anyone who sees personal worth or station is arrogant and distant from God; claiming a rank for oneself encroaches on divine lordship, since no one has independent worth before Him.
QUSHAYRI:v1p325/r4.anchor: فمن ادعى لنفسه محلا فقد نازع الربوبية

QUSHAYRI:v1p325/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p325/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p325/r7.claim: Satan openly opposed the Real after appearing wholly sincere in servitude, showing that his former conduct had not arisen from sincerity and truth.
QUSHAYRI:v1p325/r7.anchor: جاهر الحقيقة بالخلاف بعدما أظهر من نفسه غاية الخلوص في العبودية

BURHAN:v2p10/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p10/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p10/r2.claim: A divine question about why people perform an act signals blame when no answer is supplied; if an answer follows, the legal implication depends on that answer.
BURHAN:v2p10/r2.anchor: وسؤاله سبحانه عن علة الفعل نحو

BURHAN:v1p116/r13.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p116/r13.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p116/r13.claim: Al-Aʿrāf and al-Ḥijr have ألا, while Ṣād has أن without لا.
BURHAN:v1p116/r13.anchor: فى الأعراف ﴿ ما منعك ألا تسجد ﴾ وفى ص ﴿ أن تسجد ﴾

BURHAN:v2p283/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p283/r5.speaker: السكاكي
BURHAN:v2p283/r5.claim: Al-Sakkākī explains naming a cause by the name of what it wards off: ما منعك ألا تسجد means ما دعاك ألا تسجد, supporting the view that لا is not extra.
BURHAN:v2p283/r5.anchor: ذكره السكاكي وخرج عليه قوله تعالى ﴿ ما منعك ألا تسجد ﴾ يعني ما دعاك الا تسجد

BURHAN:v2p283/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p283/r6.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v2p283/r6.claim: Another explanation takes the question to mean what protected Iblīs from punishment for failing to prostrate.
BURHAN:v2p283/r6.anchor: وقيل معناه ما حماك في ألا تسجد اي من العقوبة

BURHAN:v2p283/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p283/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p283/r7.claim: The author rejects the proposed meanings as linguistically unsound or mismatched to the past-tense question, then reads the question as taunting Iblīs for acting as if secure from punishment.
BURHAN:v2p283/r7.anchor: ويجاب بأن المخالفة تقتضي الأمنه كانه قيل ما امنك حتى خالفت

BURHAN:v2p283/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p283/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p283/r8.claim: An objection says أنا خير answers why Iblīs did not prostrate, not why he did not refrain from prostrating; the reply is that he diverted to a different, unanswerable issue.
BURHAN:v2p283/r8.anchor: ورد ايضا بانه أجاب ﴿ أنا خير ﴾ وهو لايصلح جوابا الا لترك السجود

BURHAN:v3p78/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p78/r4.speaker: الشلوبين
BURHAN:v3p78/r4.claim: Al-Shalawbīn says the addition in لئلا يعلم is agreed upon and stated by Sībawayh; context requires it, as in ما منعك ألا تسجد.
BURHAN:v3p78/r4.anchor: قال الشلوبين وأما زيادة لا في قوله ﴿ لئلا يعلم أهل الكتاب ﴾ 2 فشيء متفق عليه وقد نص عليه سيبويه

BURHAN:v3p78/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p78/r8.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p78/r8.claim: The parallel wording ما منعك أن تسجد shows that لا is not a literal object of prevention; otherwise the reproach would concern merely failing to leave prostration.
BURHAN:v3p78/r8.anchor: ومنه ﴿ ما منعك ألا تسجد ﴾ 4 بدليل الاية الأخرى ﴿ ما منعك أن تسجد ﴾ 5

BURHAN:v4p357/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p357/r4.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v4p357/r4.claim: One account says لا emphasizes the semantic negation already in منعك, as the parallel ما منعك أن تسجد indicates.
BURHAN:v4p357/r4.anchor: وقيل إنما زيدت توكيدا للنفي المعنوي

BURHAN:v4p357/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p357/r5.speaker: ابن السيد
BURHAN:v4p357/r5.claim: Ibn al-Sayyid says لا follows the meaning of prevention: preventing someone means ordering that person not to act.
BURHAN:v4p357/r5.anchor: وقال ابن السيد إنما دخلت لما يقتضيه معنى المنع

BURHAN:v3p79/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p79/r1.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v3p79/r1.claim: One non-addition analysis reads ما منعك as ما دعاك: both a deterrent and a prompt can lead to the absence of an act.
BURHAN:v3p79/r1.anchor: أحدهما أن التقدير ما دعاك إلى ألا تسجد لأن الصارف عن الشيء داع إلى تركه

BURHAN:v3p79/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p79/r2.speaker: قيل
BURHAN:v3p79/r2.claim: A closer analysis supplies من before ألا تسجد; it preserves the ordinary meaning of منع and avoids positing an extra particle.
BURHAN:v3p79/r2.anchor: وهذا أقرب مما قبله لأن فيه إبقاء المنع على أصله وعدم زيادتها أولى

BURHAN:v3p79/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p79/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p79/r3.claim: Adding لا can strengthen affirmation: the affirmative meaning persists despite a particle that normally opposes it, making the assertion firmer.
BURHAN:v3p79/r3.anchor: وفائدة زيادتها تأكيد الإثبات فإن وضع لا نفي ما دخلت عليه

BURHAN:v3p110/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p110/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p110/r4.claim: Language signals ellipsis because a transitive verb such as ضربت requires an object, though the verb identifies the event without specifying the object; subjects and predicates can likewise be omitted.
BURHAN:v3p110/r4.anchor: ومنها اللغة كضربت فإن اللغة قاضية أن الفعل المتعدي لا بد له من مفعول

BURHAN:v3p110/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p110/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p110/r5.claim: Earlier wording can identify an omission: the alternative accounts of ما منعك, and بلاغ in لم يلبثوا إلا ساعة من نهار بلاغ is completed as هذا بلاغ, stated in Ibrāhīm.
BURHAN:v3p110/r5.anchor: ومنها تقدم ما يدل على المحذوف وما في سياقه

SULAMI:v1p221#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p221#3/r1.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p221#3/r1.claim: Al-Wasiti warns that relying on ritual observances in both worlds makes ignorance a home, objection a trait, and distance from God its outcome; seeing worship as one's own act is dangerous self-regard.
SULAMI:v1p221#3/r1.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : من استصحب كل نسك في الدنيا والآخرة

SULAMI:v1p221#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p221#3/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p221#3/r2.claim: One explanation says Iblis saw his substance and worship and thought himself superior; self-regard in one's acts corrupts the soul.
SULAMI:v1p221#3/r2.anchor: قال بعضهم : لما نظر إلى الجوهر والعبادة ظن أنه المسكين خير

SULAMI:v1p221#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p221#3/r3.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p221#3/r3.claim: Another says Iblis's self-assertion alone brought the curse: nothing distanced him more than seeing himself.
SULAMI:v1p221#3/r3.anchor: وقيل : لما قال إبليس : ' أنا ' قيل له : إن عليك اللعنة

SULAMI:v1p221#3/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p221#3/r4.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p221#3/r4.claim: A further gloss says Iblis mistook created substance and origin for superiority, failing to recognize that merit comes from the Bestower rather than one's essence.
SULAMI:v1p221#3/r4.anchor: وقيل في قوله ' أنا خير منه ' توهم أن الجوهر من الكون

SULAMI:v1p221#3/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p221#3/r5.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v1p221#3/r5.claim: Al-Wasiti says wearing the garment of ritual practice makes the ego's claim of I arise; even without saying better, Iblis would have been ruined by asserting I in comparison.
SULAMI:v1p221#3/r5.anchor: قال الواسطي رحمة الله عليه : من لبس قميص النسك خاصره ' أنا '

SULAMI:v1p221#3/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p221#3/r6.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p221#3/r6.claim: Ibn Ata says pride in himself veiled Iblis from revering God; when the Real dominates a heart, it leaves no room to exalt anyone else.
SULAMI:v1p221#3/r6.anchor: قال ابن عطاء في قوله : ' أنا خير منه ' : حجب إبليس برؤية الفخر بنفسه

ITQAN:v2p500/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p500/r9.speaker: ابن جني
ITQAN:v2p500/r9.claim: Ibn Jinni treats the extra lā as emphatic, equivalent in force to repeating the clause once more.
ITQAN:v2p500/r9.anchor: قال ابن جني لا هنا مؤكدة قائمة مقام إعادة الجملة مرة أخرى

ITQAN:v3p102/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p102/r2.speaker: السكاكي
ITQAN:v3p102/r2.claim: Al-Sakkaki reads ما منعك ألا تسجد as what prompted you not to prostrate, avoiding the claim that لا is redundant.
ITQAN:v3p102/r2.anchor: ذكره السكاكي وخرج عليه قوله تعالى ﴿ ما منعك ألا تسجد ﴾ يعني ما دعاك إلى ألا تسجد

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p109/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p109/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p109/r1.claim: ما ضربت إلا زيدا is sound, but fronting أنا after negation in ما أنا ضربت إلا زيدا makes the denial conflict with إلا, which asserts that the speaker did strike Zayd.
