JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p109/r1.anchor: لأن نقض النفي بإلا يقتضي أن تكون ضربت زيدا

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p109/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p109/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p109/r2.claim: With the verb first, ما ضربت زيدا denies that the speaker struck Zayd but leaves other objects open; with the object first, ما زيدا ضربت presupposes a strike and denies only that Zayd was its object.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p109/r2.anchor: فإذا قلت : ما ضربت زيدا ؛ فقدمت الفعل كان المعنى أنك قد نفيت أن يكون قد وقع ضرب منك على زيد

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p109/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p109/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p109/r3.claim: Verb-focused negation can be followed by an opposite action; object-focused negation instead needs another object as contrast, and fronted prepositional complements work the same way.

AKHFASH:v1p321/r2.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p321/r2.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p321/r2.claim: Mā manaʿaka allā tasjuda means mā manaʿaka an tasjuda; lā is an extra particle joining the speech, as the poem demonstrates.
AKHFASH:v1p321/r2.anchor: وقال {ما منعك ألا تسجد} ومعناه: ما منعك أن تسجد، و {لا} ها هنا زائدة

AKHFASH:v1p321/r3.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p321/r3.speaker: الشاعر
AKHFASH:v1p321/r3.claim: An unnamed poet's line is explained by Arabs as abā jawduhu al-bukhla, with lā as an extra connective filler.
AKHFASH:v1p321/r3.anchor: وقال الشاعر: [من الطويل وهو الشاهد الرابع بعد المئتين] : أبى جوده "لا" البخل

AKHFASH:v1p321/r4.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p321/r4.speaker: يونس
AKHFASH:v1p321/r4.claim: Yūnus reports that Abū ʿAmr read al-bukhli in the genitive, construing lā as the particle meaning no, which can signal either generosity or miserliness.
AKHFASH:v1p321/r4.anchor: وزعم يونس ان أبا عمرو كان يجر "البخل"

DAMGHANI:v1p420/r24.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p420/r24.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p420/r24.claim: The negative particle can be extra: “what prevented you from not prostrating” means “what prevented you from prostrating.”
DAMGHANI:v1p420/r24.anchor: ما منعك أن لا تسج إذ أمرتك

FARRA:v1p373/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p373/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p373/r5.claim: The intended sense is ما منعك أن تسجد; لا is an extra particle accompanying أن after a negative expression, reinforcing the negation.
FARRA:v1p373/r5.anchor: المعنى- والله أعلم- ما منعك أن تسجد. و (أن) في هذا الموضع تصحبها لا، وتكون (لا) صلة.

FARRA:v1p373/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p373/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p373/r6.claim: Arabic can repeat a negative particle for emphasis, as in ما إن رأينا; Qurʾanic parallels include the cited clauses in 6:109, 21:95, and 57:29.
FARRA:v1p373/r6.anchor: و ربما أعادوا على خبره جحدا للاستيثاق من الجحد والتوكيد له كما قالوا:

FARRA:v1p373/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p373/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p373/r7.claim: ما is nominative as the subject of the question; a syntactically explicit answer would be منعني منك أنك بخيل.
FARRA:v1p373/r7.anchor: وقوله: ما منعك (ما) في موضع رفع. ولو وضع لمثلها من الكلام جواب مصحح كان رفعا

FARRA:v1p373/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p373/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p373/r8.claim: أنا خير منه answers the intended question by implication rather than matching its construction; a fully corrected answer to كيف بت البارحة would be صالحا, not صالح.
FARRA:v1p373/r8.anchor: وهو مما ذكر جوابه على غير بناء أوله، فقال: (أنا خير منه) ولم يقل: منعني من السجود

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p165#6/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p165#6/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p165#6/r1.claim: The question means what prevented you from prostrating; lā is extra, for the reason explained in Taʾwīl Mushkil al-Qurʾān.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p165#6/r1.anchor: {ما منعك ألا تسجد إذ أمرتك} أي: أن تسجد. و"لا" زائدة للعلة التي ذكرناها في "المشكل" (3) .

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p153/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p153/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p153/r2.claim: The لا is extra; the intended question is what prevented Iblis from prostrating, with the added negative reflecting that he did not.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p153/r2.anchor: أي ما منعك أن تسجد. فزاد في الكلام (لا) لأنه لم يسجد.

MAJAZ:v1p10#2/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p10#2/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p10#2/r5.claim: He groups the cited examples as surplus letters in speech whose dropping yields the intended construction.
MAJAZ:v1p10#2/r5.anchor: ومن مجاز ما يزاد فى الكلام من حروف الزوائد، قال الله: «إن الله لا يستحيي أن يضرب مثلا ما بعوضة

MAJAZ:v1p10#2/r8.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v1p10#2/r8.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v1p10#2/r8.claim: He introduces concise phrasing that dispenses with repetition; the excerpt stops before its example.
MAJAZ:v1p10#2/r8.anchor: ومن مجاز المجمل استغناء عن التكرير قال

SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes لا as an emphatic extra particle, citing 38:75, where منعك أن تسجد occurs without it.
SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r1.anchor: قال الزمخشري: " لا " في " أن لا تسجد " صلة بدليل قوله تعالى

SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari compares لئلا يعلم in 57:29, where لا means ليعلم.
SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r2.anchor: ومثلها: لئلا يعلم أهل الكتاب [الحديد: 29] بمعنى ليعلم

SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the extra لا intensifies and confirms the action: what stopped you from making yourself prostrate when commanded?
SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r3.anchor: ثم قال: " فإن قلت: ما فائدة زيادتها؟ قلت: توكيد معنى الفعل الذي تدخل عليه

SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r4.claim: A cited poem with البخل in the accusative seems to support extra لا, but the author says that reading is not decisive because other parses are possible.
SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r4.anchor: يروى " البخل " بالنصب والجر، والنصب ظاهر الدلالة في زيادتها

SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r5.speaker: الزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r5.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses لا as an object and البخل as its بدل, since لا itself conveys withholding.

SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r6.claim: An alternative parse makes لا the object and البخل a causal object: generosity refused the word no out of aversion to miserliness.
SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r6.anchor: والثاني: أنها مفعول بها أيضا، والبخل مفعول من أجله والمعنى: أبى جوده لفظ " لا "

SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r7.speaker: أبو عمرو
SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r7.claim: Abu Amr reports البخل in the genitive, which he regards as evidence that لا is used for miserliness rather than as an extra particle.
SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r7.anchor: قال أبو عمرو بن العلاء: " الرواية فيه بخفض " البخل " لأن " لا " تستعمل في البخل

SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r8.speaker: يونس
SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r8.claim: Yunus reports Abu Amr's analysis that لا is annexed to البخل for specification; لا can also express generosity when it refuses a command to withhold.
SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r8.anchor: وحكى بعضهم عن يونس قال: " كان أبو عمرو بن العلاء يجر " البخل " ويجعل " لا " مضافة إليه

SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r9.claim: A second poem is taken to mean أفعنك برق, with لا as an extra particle.
SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r9.anchor:
وأنشدوا أيضا على زيادتها قول الآخر:
2146 أفعنك لا برق كأن وميضه

SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r10.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r10.claim: The Shaykh proposes that the poem's لا coordinates with an omitted phrase, understood as أفعنك لا عن غيرك.
SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r10.anchor: وقد خرجه الشيخ على احتمال كونها عاطفة وحذف المعطوف، والتقدير: أفعنك لا عن غيرك

SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r11.speaker: الكسائي والفراء وأبو إسحاق
SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r11.claim: Al-Kisai, al-Farra, and Abu Ishaq hold that لا is extra in the verse.
SAMIN-DURR:7:12/r11.anchor: وكون " لا " في الآية زائدة هو مذهب الكسائي والفراء وأبي إسحاق

SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r1.speaker: جماعة
SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r1.claim: Some reject the extra-particle analysis and propose an ellipsis: what prevented you and forced you not to prostrate?
SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r1.anchor: فقال بعضهم: في الكلام حذف يصح به النفي، والتقدير: ما منعك فأحوجك أن لا تسجد

SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r2.speaker: جماعة
SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r2.claim: Another paraphrase asks what compelled Iblis not to prostrate.
SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم: المعنى على ما ألجأك أن لا تسجد

SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r3.speaker: جماعة
SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r3.claim: Another paraphrase asks who ordered Iblis not to prostrate.
SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r3.anchor: وبعضهم: من أمرك أن لا تسجد

SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r4.speaker: جماعة
SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r4.claim: Another paraphrase asks who told Iblis not to prostrate.
SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r4.anchor: ومن قال لك أن لا تسجد

SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r5.speaker: جماعة
SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r5.claim: Another paraphrase asks what called Iblis not to prostrate.
SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r5.anchor: أو ما دعاك أن لا تسجد؟

SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r6.claim: The author calls these paraphrases strained and says grammatical زيادة is a technical usage, not a claim that Qur'anic words are meaningless.
SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r6.anchor: وهذا تمحل من يتحرج من نسبة الزيادة إلى القرآن وقد تقدم تحقيقه

SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r7.claim: ما is an interrogative subject and the following clause is its predicate, meaning what thing prevented you.
SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r7.anchor: استفهامية في محل رفع بالابتداء، والخبر بعدها أي: أي شيء منعك

SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r8.claim: أن is accusative or genitive after an elided preposition, understood as ما منعك من السجود.
SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r8.anchor: و " أن " في محل نصب أو جر لأنها على حذف حرف الجر إذ التقدير: ما منعك من السجود؟

SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r9.claim: إذ is an adverb attached to تسجد and identifies the time of God's command to Iblis.
SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r9.anchor: و " إذ " منصوب بتسجد أي: ما منعك من السجود في وقت أمري إياك به

SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r10.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r10.claim: The clause خلقتني من نار has no syntactic slot; it explains the content of Iblis's answer.
SAMIN-DURR:7:12#2/r10.anchor: وقوله: { خلقتني من نار } لا محل لهذه الجملة لأنها كالتفسير والبيان للخبرية

ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r2.claim: The لا is emphatic and omitted in sense, so the question means ما منعك أن تسجد.
ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r2.anchor: إلغاء " لا " وهي مؤكدة، المعنى: ما منعك أن تسجد

ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r3.claim: Although God knew the cause, the question rebukes Iblis and exposes his defiant disobedience.
ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r3.anchor: فمسألته عن هذا والله قد علم ما منعه، توبيخ له وليظهر أنه معاند

ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r4.claim: Anyone who disobeys God's command while denying that it is obligatory is an unbeliever by consensus; denying prayer's obligation is the example.
ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r4.anchor: وكل من خالف الله في أمره فلم يره واجبا عليه كافر بإجماع

ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r5.claim: Iblis's refusal was defiant unbelief, unlike Adam and Eve, who confessed their sin and repented; Iblis persisted without repentance.
ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r5.anchor: فأعلم الله جل ثناؤه أن معصية إبليس معصية معاندة وكفر

ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r6.claim: The same treatment of لا applies in لئلا يعلم أهل الكتاب, where the meaning is لأن يعلم أهل الكتاب.
ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r6.anchor: أي: لأن يعلم أهل الكتاب، وقول الشاعر:

ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r7.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r7.speaker: قالوا
ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r7.claim: For the cited verse, they explain أبى جوده لا البخل to mean that his generosity rejected miserliness.

ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r8.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r8.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r8.claim: Abu Amr reports the line as أبى جوده البخل; he explains لا as what makes a person miserly and نعم as assent to continue giving.
ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r8.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو بن العلاء: الرواية أبى جوده البخل.

ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r9.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r9.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r9.claim: Al-Zajjaj offers another parse: لا is not redundant, and البخل is accusative as a substitute for لا.
ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r9.anchor: أرى أن تكون " لا " غير لغو، وأن يكون البخل منصوبا بدلا من " لا ".

ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r10.claim: ما is nominative as the interrogative subject: what prevented you? No explicit answer is given because the question itself conveys it.
ZAJJAJ:v2p322/r10.anchor: وموضع " ما " في قوله: (ما منعك ألا تسجد) رفع، المعنى أي شيء منعك في السجود

ASAD-NOTES:7:8#n10/r6.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:7:8#n10/r6.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:7:8#n10/r6.claim: Asad points to his note on 38:76 for Iblis's claim in the next verse that he was created from fire.
ASAD-NOTES:7:8#n10/r6.anchor: As regards Iblis' statement, in the next verse, that he had been created "out of fire", see surah 38. note 60.

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13/r3.claim: Araf adds an emphatic extra lā to the question about prostration, whereas Sad asks without it; the author says Araf’s account calls for stronger emphasis.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13/r3.anchor: فقد زاد (لا) في الأعراف لتوكيد السجود وهو قوله: (ألاّ تسجد) دون ما ورد في (ص)

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13/r4.claim: Araf’s story opens with the emphatic “Indeed, We created you,” while Sad’s begins “When We said”; the author takes this as evidence of Araf’s stronger emphasis.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13/r4.anchor: أن التوكيد في قصة الأعراف أشد فاقتضى ذلك أن يؤتى بـ (لا) الزائدة المؤكدة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13/r6.claim: The Araf story accumulates emphatic forms, including “you are among the humbled,” Satan’s emphatic threats, and his oath to Adam’s pair, further suiting the extra lā.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13/r6.anchor: وأن المؤكدات فيها أكثر (لقد، زيادة (لا) ، إنك من الصاغرين

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13/r7.claim: Araf explicitly recalls the command, unlike Sad’s “to what I created with My two hands”; the author says disobeying that command makes the reckoning harsher and the wording more severe.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13/r7.anchor: مما حسّن التأكيد واقتضاه في الأعراف قوله: {إِذْ أَمَرْتُكَ} ومخالفة هذا الأمر كبيرة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13/r8.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13/r8.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13/r8.claim: The opening disjointed letters of Araf are alif, lām, and ṣād; earlier scholars observed that a surah’s opening letters recur in it more prominently, so the extra lā (lām and alif) fits Araf.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13/r8.anchor: فناسب ذلك زيادة (لا) وهي لام وألف في السورة التي تبدأ بألف ولام دون التي لم تبدأ بهما

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13/r9.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13/r9.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13/r9.claim: Prostration derivatives occur nine times in Araf and three times in Sad; Araf’s final verse also says the angels prostrate, while Sad uses these forms only in Adam’s story, supporting extra emphasis in Araf.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13/r9.anchor: ذلك أن مشتقات السجود كالسجود والساجدين ونحوها ترددت

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13/r10.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13/r10.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13/r10.claim: The greater divine anger in Araf also calls for stronger emphasis and harsher wording than in Sad.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13/r10.anchor: ثم إن مقام السخط والغضب في قصة الأعراف أكبر كما ذكرنا، فناسب ذلك الزيادة في التوكيد والغلظة في القول

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13/r11.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13/r11.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13/r11.claim: Araf omits Iblis’s name from the question, while Sad names him; the author cites this as a sign of Araf’s greater anger.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13/r11.anchor: أنه طوى اسم إبليس فلم يذكره في الأعراف فقال: {قَالَ مَا مَنَعَكَ أَلَّا تَسْجُدَ} في حين ذكر اسمه في (ص)

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13#2/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13#2/r1.claim: Al-Aʿraf’s scene conveys greater divine displeasure than the account in Ṣād, shown by the briefer exchange with Iblis.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13#2/r1.anchor: عدم التبسط مع إبليس في الكلام بخلاف ما ورد في (ص)

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13#2/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13#2/r2.claim: In al-Aʿraf God asks only what prevented Iblis from prostrating when commanded; in Ṣād He addresses him by name and adds the created-by-My-hands and arrogance questions.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13#2/r2.anchor: قَالَ ياإبليس مَا مَنَعَكَ أَن تَسْجُدَ لِمَا خَلَقْتُ بِيَدَيَّ أَسْتَكْبَرْتَ أَمْ كُنتَ مِنَ العالين

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13#2/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13#2/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13#2/r3.claim: In Ṣād Iblis asks for respite with “Lord” and an introductory fa; in al-Aʿraf he asks without either addition.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13#2/r3.anchor: قَالَ رَبِّ فأنظرني إلى يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13#2/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13#2/r4.claim: Ṣād’s answer adds fa and specifies the appointed time, while al-Aʿraf’s answer omits both additions.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13#2/r4.anchor: قَالَ فَإِنَّكَ مِنَ المنظرين * إلى يَوْمِ الوقت المعلوم

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13#2/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13#2/r5.claim: In Ṣād, the response mirrors Iblis’s request by repeating fa; al-Aʿraf omits fa in both request and answer.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13#2/r5.anchor: ثم انظر من الناحية الفنية كيف أنه في (ص) لما ذكر الفاء في قوله: {قَالَ رَبِّ فأنظرني} كان الجواب بالفاء كذلك

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13#2/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13#2/r6.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13#2/r6.claim: Iblis speaks more expansively in Ṣād when God’s speech is expansive; under al-Aʿraf’s greater displeasure, Iblis keeps his reply to its shortest form.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r13#2/r6.anchor: لما رأى أن الله يبسّط معه في الكلام تبسّط هو أيضاً، بخلاف ما في الأعراف فإنه لما رأى السخط الكبير

SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.claim: Some verbs can take two direct objects, though a speaker may stop after the first or continue with a second object.
SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.anchor: الذي يتعداه فعله إلى مفعولين فإن شئت اقتصرت على المفعول الأول

SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.claim: Choosing someone from a group can take two direct objects after the preposition is omitted; Sībawayh cites Qur'an 7:155 as an example.

SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.claim: Naming and giving a kunya can take two objects; daʿawtuhu takes two only when it means naming, while calling someone to an action takes one.

SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.claim: Many such verbs originally govern a phrase introduced by a preposition; when the preposition is omitted, the verb governs the complement directly.

SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.claim: An unnamed poet's astaghfiru Allāha dhanban represents astaghfiru Allāha min dhanbin, with min omitted.

SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.claim: ʿAmr b. Maʿdīkarib's amartuka al-khayr means amartuka bi-l-khayr, with bāʾ omitted.
SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.anchor: أمرتك الخير فافعل ما أمرت به

SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.claim: Al-Mutalammis's ālaytu ḥubb al-ʿIrāq means ālaytu ʿalā ḥubb al-ʿIrāq, with ʿalā omitted.

SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.claim: Nubbiʾtu Zaydan means 'I was told about Zayd'; ʿan and ʿalā do not omit like bāʾ, nor does min in a positive clause.
SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.anchor: وكما تقول نبئت زيدا يقول ذاك أي عن زيد وليست عن وعلى

SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.claim: Astaghfiru Allāha dhanban and amartuka al-khayr are uncommon constructions used only by some speakers.

SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.claim: With sammaytu and kannaytu, bāʾ works as in ʿaraftuhu bi-Zaydin; the prepositional construction differs in meaning from the direct-object construction.

SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.claim: Al-Farazdaq's ikhtīra al-rijāla shows the direct-object construction with ikhtāra.

SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.claim: Al-Farazdaq also uses nubbiʾtu ʿAbda Allāhi bi-l-jawwi as an example of a verb taking its complement through bāʾ.

SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.claim: This treatment is limited: verbs do not all permit preposition deletion, and verbs do not all take one or two objects.
SIBAWAYH:الذييتعداهفعلهإلىمفعولينفإنشئتا.anchor: كما أنه ليس كل فعل يتعدى الفاعل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.claim: Ailments commonly use faʿila yafʿalu, with a verbal noun on faʿal and an adjective on faʿil; Sībawayh illustrates the pattern with ḥabiṭa and ḥabija.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.anchor: وذلك حبط يحبط حبطا وهو حبط وحبج يحبج حبجا وهو حبج

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.claim: The adjective may instead be faʿīl, as in mariḍa yamraḍu and marīḍ.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.anchor: نحو مرض يمرض مرضا وهو مريض

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.claim: Saqima may be said with kasra or by some Arabs with fatḥa, compared with karuma and karīm.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.anchor: وقالوا سقم يسقم سقما وهو سقيم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.claim: Saqm and ḥuzn are verbal nouns; ḥuzn is grouped with disease because it is an affliction.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.anchor: جعلوه بمنزلة المرض لأنه داء

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.claim: Wajila and similar states of fear follow the same verb and noun pattern because they are close in meaning to wajiʿa.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.anchor: وقرب المعنى وجل يوجل وجلا وهو وجل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.claim: Blindness of the heart is treated as an affliction that strikes the heart.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.anchor: إنما جعله بلاء أصاب قلبه

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.claim: Fear and terror verbs such as faziʿa, fariqa, wajila, and wajira use this pattern because fear reaches the heart as illness reaches the body.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.anchor: لأنه داء قد وصل إلى فؤاده

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.claim: Awjara joins the faʿila pattern in a related sense; faʿila and afʿala can coexist, as in other paired adjective patterns.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.anchor: فأدخلوا أفعل ههنا على فعل لأن فعلا وأفعل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.claim: Farriqtuhu and fazzaʿtuhu mean farriqtu minhu and faziʿtu minhu; the preposition min has been omitted.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.anchor: كما قالوا أمرتك الخير

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.claim: Khashiyahu, khashyatan, and khāsh follow a derivational pattern like raḥima and rāḥim, even though the surface forms differ.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.anchor: وقالوا خشيته خشية وهو خاش كما قالوا رحم وهو راحم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.claim: Opposite states such as arisha, batira, fariḥa, and jaḏila use the same verb, noun, and adjective pattern.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.anchor: أشر يأشر أشرا وهو أشر

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.claim: Forms such as jaḏlān, kaslān, and sakrān pair with jaḏil, kasil, and sakir, showing related faʿlān and faʿil formations.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.anchor: وقالوا جذلان كما قالوا كسلان وكسل وسكران وسكر

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.claim: Nashiṭa has the adjective nashīṭ, while nashāṭ parallels suqām; saqīm and suqām are compared with jamīl and jamāl.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.anchor: وقالوا نشط ينشط وهو نشيط

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.claim: Defects such as sahk and qinam are treated like diseases, with corresponding nouns sahka and qinma.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.anchor: وقالوا سهك يسهك سهكا وهو سهك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.claim: ʿAqara and ʿāqir follow the same pattern as saqima and sāqim, and māthik provides a parallel adjective.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.anchor: وقالوا عقرت عقرا كما قالوا سقمت

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.claim: Khamaṭ is contrasted with qinam, which Sībawayh glosses as sahk.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.anchor: وقالوا خمط خمطا وهو خمط

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.claim: Arija describes wind movement and brightness, while ḥamisa describes agitation and anger; these share a semantic group of arousal.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.anchor: وذلك قولهم أرج يأرج أرجا وهو أرج

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.claim: Aḥmasa occurs alongside ḥamisa; in this group afʿal functions like faʿlān, as in ghaḍbān.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.anchor: وصار أفعل ههنا بمنزلة فعلان وغضبان

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.claim: Afʿal can also join faʿlān forms and generally keeps the same verb and verbal-noun pattern.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.anchor: فلا يفارقهما في بناء الفعل والمصدر كثيرا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.speaker: أبو الخطاب
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.claim: Abū al-Khaṭṭāb reports that ahyam and haymān both mean thirsty.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.anchor: رجل أهيم وهيمان يريدون شيئا واحدا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.claim: Salis, qaliq, naziq, and ghaliq are grouped with agitation because they denote lightness and movement.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.anchor: قلق يقلق قلقا وهو قلق

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.claim: Ghaliq can describe nonhuman things too, since they have become light or loose in their place.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.anchor: وكذلك الغلق في غير الأناسي لأنه قد خف من مكانه

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.claim: Unpleasant qualities such as ʿasr, shakās, laqas, and laḥaz follow faʿila yafʿalu with faʿil adjectives because their meanings resemble ailments.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.anchor: لتقاربها في المعنى وذلك ما تعذر عليك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.claim: Saqima and ʿasura can both yield faʿīl adjectives; nakida has both nakid and an-kad, and laḥija is close in meaning to ʿasura.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.anchor: وقد قالوا عسر الأمر وهو عسير كما قالوا سقم وهو سقيم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.claim: Laḥija is included in the same group because its meaning is close to ʿusr.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابماجاءمنالأدواءعلىمثالوجع.anchor: لأن معناه قريب من معنى العسر

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p714/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p714/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p714/r1.claim: The general command in Baqara is addressed to the angels, while Iblis received a separate, specific command in al-Aʿrāf; he need not be counted among the angels commanded there.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p714/r1.anchor: فليس بالضرورة أن الله تعالى أمر إبليس بالسجود مع الملائكة لكنه تعالى أمر الملائكة بالسجود

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p799/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p799/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p799/r5.claim: Iblis was commanded separately as well as the angels collectively: the author reads the angels’ general order in Baqara and a specific order to Iblis in al-Aʿrāf.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p846/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p846/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p846/r1.claim: In al-Aʿrāf, lā is emphatic and nonnegative: reading it as negation would make God reproach Iblis for prostrating, while the charge is his failure to prostrate; Ṭā Hā uses a similar construction.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p846/r1.anchor: إذن (لا) مزيدة للتوكيد جيء بها لغرض التوكيد لأن المعلوم أن يحاسبه على عدم السجود

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p588/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p588/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p588/r4.claim: Lā may be an emphatic connective when ambiguity is impossible; al-Aʿrāf’s rebuking context and frequent prostration support its use in this question.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p588/r4.anchor: هناك قاعدة (لا) يمكن أن تُزاد إذا أُمن اللبس، وسُمّيت حرف صلة وغرضها التوكيد وليس النفي

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p847/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p847/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p847/r1.claim: Al-Aʿrāf has more emphatic forms, a longer Adam account, and more prostration-root forms than Ṣād; Samarrai says this context makes the added lā fitting.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p847/r1.anchor: ثم إن مشتقات السجود في سورة الأعراف أكثر (9 مرات) أما في سورة ص (3 مرات)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p847/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p847/r2.speaker: القدامى
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p847/r2.claim: Earlier scholars observed that the disconnected opening letters stamp a sūra with a characteristic letter pattern, reflected in its vocabulary.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p847/r2.anchor: انتبه له القدامى في السور التي تبدأ بالأحرف المقطعة وهي أن هذه الأحرف تطبع السورة بطابعها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p847/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p847/r3.speaker: جعفر بن الزبير
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p847/r3.claim: Jaʿfar ibn al-Zubayr counted the sequence alif-lām-rāʾ 220 times in its sūra.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p847/r3.anchor: جعفر بن الزبير أحصى ورود الر 220 مرة في السورة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p847/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p847/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p847/r4.claim: Because al-Aʿrāf opens with alif-lām-mīm-ṣād and the added lā uses lām and alif, Samarrai finds the wording suited to the sūra’s opening letters as well as its context.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p847/r4.anchor: وفي الآية موضع السؤال اللام والألف وهما أحرف (لا) فناسب ذكر (لا) في آية سورة الأعراف

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p847/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p847/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p847/r5.claim: As a usage correction, Samarrai says one should say I apologize for not attending, not I apologize for attending.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p847/r5.anchor: مثلاً من الخطأ الشائع أننا نقول أعتذر عن الحضور وإنما الصحيح القول: أعتذر عن عدم الحضور.

ALUSI-FULL:v8p87#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p87#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p87#2/r1.claim: The opening “he said” resumes the narrative to answer an implied question about God’s response to Iblīs’s failure to prostrate; the shift to third person also distances the report from its hearers.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p87#2/r1.anchor: استئناف مسوق للجواب عن سؤال نشأ من حكاية عدم سجوده

ALUSI-FULL:v8p87#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p87#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p87#2/r2.claim: Most grammarians treat lā as extra, supported by 38:75 and by the analogous usage in “so that the People of the Book may know”; it intensifies and confirms the verb.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p87#2/r2.anchor: المشهور أن ( لا ) مزيدة بدليل قوله سبحانه في آية أخرى

ALUSI-FULL:v8p87#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p87#2/r3.speaker: الشهاب
ALUSI-FULL:v8p87#2/r3.claim: Al-Shihāb says lā does not intensify universally; with an explicit or implicit negation it emphasizes that the prohibition attached to the refusal, marking the omission as the offense.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p87#2/r3.anchor: قال الشهاب : والذي يظهر لي أنها لا تؤكده مطلقا بل إذا صحب نفيا

ALUSI-FULL:v8p87#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p87#2/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v8p87#2/r4.claim: An alternative takes “prevent” figuratively as compel: what forced you not to prostrate? Al-Sakkākī instead describes it as a metaphor for what carried or urged Iblīs to refuse; the readings differ little.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p87#2/r4.anchor: وقيل : إنها غير زائدة بان يكون المنع مجازا عن الالجاء والاضطرار

ALUSI-FULL:v8p87#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p87#2/r5.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v8p87#2/r5.claim: Al-Rāghib distinguishes prevention as stinginess from protection; here it means protection from not prostrating, i.e. what kept Iblīs from the refusal.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p87#2/r5.anchor: وقال الراغب المنع يقال في ضد العطية كرجل مانع ومناع

ALUSI-FULL:v8p87#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p87#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p87#2/r6.claim: “When” is an adverb attached to “prostrate.” The verse is cited for the view that commands require immediate compliance because Iblīs is blamed for failing to act promptly.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p87#2/r6.anchor: و ( إذ ) ظرف لتسجد وهذ الآية أحد أدلة القائلين بأن الأمر للفور

ALUSI-FULL:v8p87#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p87#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p87#2/r7.claim: One reply locates immediacy in the preceding command “fall prostrate”; some deny that the result particle necessarily entails immediate succession, while another argument relies on blame for violating an unqualified command.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p87#2/r7.anchor: وأجيب بأن الفور إنما هو من قوله تعالى : ( فقعوا له ساجدين )

ALUSI-FULL:v8p87#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p87#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p87#2/r8.claim: The different forms of divine reproach across the sūras imply that Iblīs combined several sins, each independently sufficient for blame; other tellings omit the reproach, and its wisdom belongs to God.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p87#2/r8.anchor: وفي حكاية التوبيخ ههنا بهذه العبارة وفي سورة الحجر

ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r1.claim: The repeated “he said” answers an implied question about Iblīs’s reply. His answer is foolishly mismatched: asked what prevented him, he answers who is better, implying the superior should not bow to an inferior.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r1.anchor: استئناف كما تقدم مبني على سؤال نشأ من حكاية التوبيخ كأنه قيل فماذا قال اللعين

ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r2.claim: Iblīs is portrayed as the first to establish arrogant self-aggrandizement and to invent rational moral judgments of good and evil.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r2.anchor: فاللعين أول من أسس بنيان التكبر واخترع القول بالحسن والقبح العليين

ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r3.claim: Iblīs argues that fire is a nobler, luminous, powerful, life-associated element, whereas clay is its opposite; he assumes nobler origin makes a nobler creature who need not obey an inferior.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r3.anchor: وحاصله اني مخلوق من عنصر أشرف من عنصره لأن عنصري علوي نير قوي التأثير مناسب لمادة الحياة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r4.claim: Al-Ālūsī rejects the ranking: each of the four elements has necessary benefits and its own virtue; earth offers more benefit and settledness, while fire’s lightness suggests rashness and pride.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r4.anchor: فان كون النار أشرف من التراب ممنوع فان كل عنصر من العناصر الأربع يختص بفوائد ليست لغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r5.claim: Nobility of origin does not guarantee nobility of offspring; thorn trees bear fruit and a narcissus grows from a bulb, while an unbeliever may descend from a believer.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r5.anchor: وأيضا شرف الأصل لايوجب شرف الفرع إنما الورد من الشوك ولا ينبت النرجس إلا من بصل

ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r6.claim: Iblīs wrongly limits honor to material origin; Adam is also honored by his Maker, end, and form: created by God’s hands, given His spirit, and appointed vicegerent.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r6.anchor: مع أن الشيء كما يشرف بمادته وعنصره يشرف بفاعله وغايته وصورته

ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r7.speaker: ظافر الاسكندري
ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r7.claim: Ẓāfir al-Iskandarī’s verse says the angels’ prostration to Adam was, in interpretation, prostration to God; serving a superior humbly is no disgrace.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r7.anchor: وإلى هذا أشار ظافر الاسكندري بقوله : أنت المراد بنظم كل قصيدة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r8.claim: The apparent reading is that Iblīs accepted the command, making his reply an even clearer objection to the wise Lord; some instead say he exempted himself from the general command by analogy.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r8.anchor: ثم الظاهر أن هذا الجواب من اللعين كان مع تسليم أنه مأمور بالسجود

ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r9.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r9.claim: Those who say Iblīs did not accept being commanded cite the rebuke against specifying a textual command by analogy; the response is that his act nullified the text altogether, though al-Ālūsī sees room for discussion.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p88/r9.anchor: واستدل أهل هذا القول بهذأ التوبيخ على أنه لايجوز تخصيص النص بالقياس

ALUSI-FULL:v8p89/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p89/r1.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
ALUSI-FULL:v8p89/r1.claim: Abū Nuʿaym and al-Daylamī report from Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad, through his father and grandfather, that the Prophet called Iblīs the first to reason about religion by personal opinion; Jaʿfar says such a reasoner is paired with Iblīs at resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p89/r1.anchor: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال أول من قاس أمر الدين برأيه إبليس

ALUSI-FULL:v8p89/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p89/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p89/r2.claim: The report is used to prohibit analogy absolutely, but the blame concerns analogy against an explicit text or analogy lacking a required condition; its full treatment belongs elsewhere.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p89/r2.anchor: بأن المذموم هو القياس والرأي في مقابلة النص أو الذي يعدم فيه شرط من الشروط المعتبرة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p89/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p89/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v8p89/r3.claim: The verse supports creation and corruption: it indicates the creation of Adam and Iblīs, the transformation of clay and fire through composition, and that Iblīs and similar beings are originated bodies, not pre-eternal spirits.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p89/r3.anchor: وفي الآية دليل على الكون والفساد لدلالتها على خلق آدم عليه السلام وإبليس عليه اللعنة

ALUSI-FULL:v8p89/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v8p89/r4.speaker: بعضهم
ALUSI-FULL:v8p89/r4.claim: Some explain that Adam is attributed to clay and Iblīs to fire because each has that element as its dominant constituent; otherwise bodies are composed of all four elements.
ALUSI-FULL:v8p89/r4.anchor: قيل : لعل اضافة خلق آدم عليه السلام إلى الطين وخلقه إلى النار باعتبار الجزء الغالب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p216#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p216#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p216#2/r6.claim: The question means “What prevented you from prostrating?”; لا is redundant, as in 21:95.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p216#2/r6.anchor: {قال} الله تعالى يا إبليس: {ما منعك ألا تسجد إذ أمرتك} أي: وما منعك أن تسجد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p216#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p216#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p216#2/r7.claim: Iblis claims superiority because God created him from fire and Adam from clay, supposing fire better and brighter than clay.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p216#2/r7.anchor: لأنك {خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين} والنار خير وأنور من الطين.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p216#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p216#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p216#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas calls Iblis the first to reason by analogy and err, and says whoever reasons about religion from personal opinion is paired with Iblis.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p216#2/r8.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أول من قاس إبليس فأخطأ القياس، فمن قاس الدين بشيء من رأيه قرنه الله مع إبليس.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p216#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p216#2/r9.speaker: ابن سيرين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p216#2/r9.claim: Ibn Sirin says the sun was worshipped only because of analogical reasoning.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p216#2/r9.anchor: قال ابن سيرين: ما عبدت الشمس إلا بالقياس.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p216#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p216#2/r10.speaker: محمد بن جرير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p216#2/r10.claim: Ibn Jarir rejects Iblis’s assumption: merit belongs to whom God grants it; clay’s weight, composure, forbearance, and patience led Adam to repentance and humility, bringing selection and guidance.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p216#2/r10.anchor: قال محمد بن جرير: ظن الخبيث أن النار خير من الطين ولم يعلم أن الفضل لمن جعل الله له الفضل، وقد فضل الله الطين على النار من وجوه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p216#2/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p216#2/r11.speaker: محمد بن جرير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p216#2/r11.claim: Ibn Jarir contrasts fire’s lightness, rashness, sharpness, and loftiness, which prompted Iblis’s arrogance and led to curse and misery.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p216#2/r11.anchor: ومن جوهر النار الخفة والطيش والحدة والارتفاع وهو الداعي لإبليس بعد الشقاوة التي سبقت له إلى الاستكبار والإصرار،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p216#2/r12.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p216#2/r12.speaker: محمد بن جرير
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p216#2/r12.claim: Ibn Jarir adds that clay gathers things whereas fire scatters them, and soil sustains life in plants while fire causes destruction.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p216#2/r12.anchor: ولأن الطين سبب جمع الأشياء والنار سبب تفرقها ولأن التراب سبب الحياة، فإن حياة الأشجار والنبات به، والنار سبب الهلاك.

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:11-12/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:11-12/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:11-12/r4.claim: The extra lā reinforces the verb and highlights the censured omission; alternatively, the question asks what forced Iblis not to prostrate.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:11-12/r4.anchor: ولا صلة مثلها في لئلا يعلم، مؤكدة معنى الفعل

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:11-12/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:11-12/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:11-12/r5.claim: The wording is evidence that an unqualified command entails obligation and immediacy.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:11-12/r5.anchor: دليل على أن مطلق الأمر للوجوب والفور

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:11-12/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:11-12/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:11-12/r6.claim: Iblis considered himself superior and could not imagine a superior being ordered to bow to an inferior; he originated arrogance and rational good-and-evil doctrine.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:11-12/r6.anchor: هو الذي سن التكبر وقال بالحسن والقبح العقليين أولا

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:11-12/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:11-12/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:11-12/r7.claim: Iblis wrongly measured merit by material origin, ignoring direct creation, form, and purpose; Adam’s knowledge and distinctive qualities explain the command to bow.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:11-12/r7.anchor: بأن رأى الفضل كله باعتبار العنصر وغفل عما يكون باعتبار الفاعل

BAYDAWI-FULL:7:11-12/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:11-12/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:11-12/r8.claim: The passage indicates generation and corruption and that devils are created bodies; Adam’s clay and Satan’s fire may be their dominant constituents.
BAYDAWI-FULL:7:11-12/r8.anchor: دليل الكون والفساد وأن الشياطين أجسام كائنة

DURR-FULL:v3p424/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p424/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v3p424/r7.claim: Qatada says Iblis envied Adam’s honor; pride and envy began sins, and God destroyed Iblis for refusing to prostrate out of pride.
DURR-FULL:v3p424/r7.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {قال أنا خير منه خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين} قال: حسد عدو الله إبليس

DURR-FULL:v3p424/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p424/r8.speaker: أبو صالح
DURR-FULL:v3p424/r8.claim: Abu Salih says Iblis was created from the fire of might and the angels from the light of might.
DURR-FULL:v3p424/r8.anchor: عن أبي صالح قال: خلق إبليس من نار العزة وخلقت الملائكة من نور العزة

DURR-FULL:v3p424/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p424/r9.speaker: الحسن
DURR-FULL:v3p424/r9.claim: Hasan says Iblis reasoned by analogy and was the first to do so.
DURR-FULL:v3p424/r9.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله {خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين} قال: قاس إبليس وهو أول من قاس

DURR-FULL:v3p424/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p424/r10.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v3p424/r10.claim: A report from the Prophet calls Iblis the first to judge a religious matter by his own opinion, citing his comparison of fire and clay.
DURR-FULL:v3p424/r10.anchor: عن جعفر بن محمد عن جده أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: أول من قاس أمر الدين برأيه إبليس

DURR-FULL:v3p424/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v3p424/r11.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
DURR-FULL:v3p424/r11.claim: Ja'far says whoever applies analogy to religion by personal opinion will be joined to Iblis at the Resurrection because he followed him in analogy.
DURR-FULL:v3p424/r11.anchor: قال جعفر: فمن قاس أمر الدين برأيه قرنه الله تعالى يوم القيامة بإبليس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p35#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p35#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p35#2/r9.claim: The passage embeds a warning that Satan has been humanity's enemy from the beginning, preparing readers for the warning in 7:27 and urging them away from the shirk and error he instigated.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p35#2/r9.anchor: وأدمج في هذا الامتنان تنبيه وإيقاظ إلى عداوة الشيطان لنوع الإنسان من القدم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p35#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p35#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p35#2/r10.claim: This episode serves the surah's aim: warning against Satan's temptation and deception and drawing people away from the shirk and misguidance he caused.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p35#2/r10.anchor: فلذلك كان هذا بمنزلة الاستدلال وسط في خلال الموعظة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p39#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p39#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p39#2/r3.claim: The change from ‘We said’ to ‘He said’ is an iltifāt: God is understood as speaker, while the discourse shifts from addressing the angels to rebuking Iblis alone.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p39#2/r3.anchor: وكان مقتضى الظاهر أن يقال : قلنا ، فكان العدول إلى ضمير الغائب التفاتا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p39#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p39#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p39#2/r4.claim: The interrogative is genuinely a question but is tinged with reproach, and its purpose is to expose Iblis’s motive to the angels.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p39#2/r4.anchor: و { ما } للاستفهام ، وهو استفهام ظاهره حقيقي ، ومشوب بتوبيخ

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p39#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p39#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p39#2/r5.claim: The expected construction would be ‘what prevented you from prostrating’; the added lā is unexpected because Iblis was prevented from bowing, not from not bowing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p39#2/r5.anchor: فكان مقتضى الظاهر أن يقال : ما منعك أن تسجد لأنه إنما كف عن السجود لا عن نفي السجود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p39#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p39#2/r6.speaker: الكسائي، والفراء، والزجاج، والزمخشري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p39#2/r6.claim: They take lā as an emphatic extra particle with no negative force, comparing emphatic constructions in 90:1, 57:29, and 21:95.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p39#2/r6.anchor: وهذا تأويل الكسائي ، والفراء ، والزجاج ، والزمخشري

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p39#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p39#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p39#2/r7.claim: Ibn Ashur rejects the emphatic-extra reading because emphasis normally confirms that an action occurred, whereas Iblis’s prostration did not occur.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p39#2/r7.anchor: فلا ينبغي التعويل على هذا التأويل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p40/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p40/r1.speaker: السكاكي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p40/r1.claim: Al-Sakkaki reads lā as negative and understands an implied opposite action: preventing someone from bowing prompts him not to bow; thus manaʿaka is metaphorically ‘prompted you.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p40/r1.anchor: وهذا تأويل السكاكي في ( المفتاح ) في فصل المجاز اللغوي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p40/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p40/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p40/r2.claim: He considers the metaphorical ‘prompted you’ interpretation, also attributed to Abd al-Jabbar by al-Fakhr, a better explanation than treating lā as an emphatic extra.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p40/r2.anchor: وقريب منه لعبد الجبار فيما نقله الفخر عنه ، وهو أحسن تأويلا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p40/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p40/r3.speaker: الطبري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p40/r3.claim: Al-Tabari instead explains the construction as ellipsis: two verbs are intended, one stated and the other omitted but indicated by its complement.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p40/r3.anchor: وأما أن يكون قد أريد الفعلان ، فذكر أحدهما وحذف الآخر ، وأشير إلى المحذوف بمتعلقه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p40/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p40/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p40/r4.claim: He refers readers to his discussion of the parallel question to Aaron in 20:92–93.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p40/r4.anchor: وانظر ما قلته عند قوله تعالى : { قال يا هارون ما منعك إذ رأيتهم ضلوا أن لا تتبعني

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p40/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p40/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p40/r5.claim: The time phrase modifies ‘prostrate’; its attachment to God’s command means the command to the angels included Iblis.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p40/r5.anchor: وتعليق ضميره بالأمر يقتضي أن أمر الملائكة شامل له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p40/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p40/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p40/r6.claim: One view makes Iblis a class of angels, created as the progenitor of jinn with a capacity for sin; this is the Quran’s apparent sense and the view of many jurists, citing 18:50.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p40/r6.anchor: وهذا هو ظاهر القرآن ، وإليه ذهب كثير من الفقهاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p40/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p40/r7.speaker: المعتزلة وبعض الأشاعرة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p40/r7.claim: Another view treats jinn as a distinct immaterial kind and Iblis as their progenitor, included among the angels for the command; Muslim’s report from Aisha says angels were created from light and jinn from fire. Ibn Ashur allows fire as light mixed with matter and angelic light as immaterial.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p40/r7.anchor: وإلى هذا ذهب المعتزله وبعض الأشاعرة ، وقد يكون المراد من النار نورا مخلوطا بالمادة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p40/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p40/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p40/r8.claim: The answer is set as dialogue; Iblis identifies his perceived superiority as the reason for refusing God’s command, making the refusal an explicit sin.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p40/r8.anchor: وهذا معصية صريحة ، وقوله : { أنا خير منه } مسوق مساق التعليل للامتناع

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p41#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p41#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p41#3/r1.claim: The clause ‘You created me from fire’ explains and clarifies Iblis’s claim that he is better than Adam.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p41#3/r1.anchor: وجملة : { خلقتني من نار } بيان لجملة : { أنا خير منه } فلذلك فصلت

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p41#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p41#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p41#3/r2.claim: Iblis could have learned his origin from angels who witnessed his creation or from God; 55:14–15 confirms that jinn were made from fire, and 18:50 identifies Iblis as a jinn.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p41#3/r2.anchor: وحصل لإبليس العلم بكونه مخلوقا من نار ، بإخبار من الملائكة الذين شهدوا خلقه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p41#3/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p41#3/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p41#3/r3.claim: Iblis grounds his self-ranking in the supposed superiority of his material element, fire, over Adam’s element, earth.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p41#3/r3.anchor: واستند في تفضيل نفسه إلى فضيلة العنصر الذي خلق منه على العنصر الذي خلق منه آدم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p41#3/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p41#3/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p41#3/r4.claim: Fire seems superior to soil through its force, dominance, light, and purity; both nevertheless contribute to living bodies. Angelic light is purer than fire’s material rays, while clay is earth mixed with life-supporting water.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p41#3/r4.anchor: والنار أفضل من التراب لقوة تأثيرها وتسلطها على الأجسام التي تلاقيها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p41#3/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p41#3/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p41#3/r5.claim: God knew Adam deserved the command through a capacity for angelic purity; raw elemental nobility alone does not determine merit, since the creator’s arrangement and the capacities it produces matter.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p41#3/r5.anchor: فأما إبليس فغره زكاء عنصره وذلك ليس كافيا في التفضيل وحده

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p41#3/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p41#3/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p41#3/r6.claim: Iblis’s fiery constitution drives destructive, impulsive action, whereas Adam’s earthy constitution supports good and chosen growth; angels’ luminous constitution inclines them by nature to pure good without deliberation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p41#3/r6.anchor: وركب آدم من عنصر التراب على هيئة تجعله يستخدم آثار القوة العنصرية في الخبر والصلاح

IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p41#3/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p41#3/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p41#3/r7.claim: Human ascent to angelic virtues is especially remarkable and descent to satanic vice especially easy; this is why humans are addressed with moral obligations.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v8p41#3/r7.anchor: ولذلك كان بلوغ الإنسان إلى الفضائل الملكية أعلى وأعجب ، وكان مبلغه إلى الرذائل الشيطانية أحط وأسهل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378/r9.speaker: الزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378/r9.claim: Al-Zajjaj calls the exception detached, but says Iblis was commanded to prostrate, as 7:12 confirms.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378/r9.anchor: فقال الزجاج هو استثناء ليس من الأول ولكن إبليس أمر بالسجود بدليل قوله تعالى: ما منعك ألا تسجد إذ أمرتك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378/r10.speaker: غير الزجاج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378/r10.claim: Others treat the exception as connected; otherwise they must posit a different mode of command to Iblis, which is weak.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p378/r10.anchor: وقال غير الزجاج: الاستثناء من الأول لأنا لو جعلناه منقطعا على قول من قال إن إبليس لم يكن من الملائكة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r2.speaker: الكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r2.claim: Al-Kisa'i treats lā as extra, yielding the meaning what prevented you from prostrating?
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r2.anchor: قال الكسائي لا هاهنا زائدة والمعنى ما منعك أن تسجد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r3.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj says mā is nominative and means what thing prevented you from prostrating; lā is emphatic.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r3.anchor: وقال الزجاج موصع ما رفع والمعنى أي شيء منعك من السجود ولا زائدة مؤكدة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r4.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r4.claim: Ibn Qutayba says lā can be extra where context conveys refusal or denial, citing three other Qur'anic constructions.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r4.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة وقد تزاد لا في الكلام والمعنى طرحها لإباء في الكلام أو جحد كهذه الآية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r5.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r5.claim: Al-Farra' treats lā as genuine negation: the prohibition is understood through the utterance, with أن introducing its implied wording.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r5.anchor: وقال الفراء لا هاهنا جحد محض وليست بزائدة والمنع راجع إلى تأويل القول

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r6.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r6.claim: Ibn Jarir supplies an ellipsis: what prevented you from prostrating, making you need not to prostrate?
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r6.anchor: وقال ابن جرير في الكلام محذوف تقديره ما منعك من السجود فأحوجك أن لا تسجد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r7.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r7.claim: Al-Zajjaj says God's question rebukes Iblis and exposes his defiance; Iblis answers the implied comparison rather than the literal question.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r7.anchor: قال الزجاج وسؤال الله تعالى لإبليس ما منعك توبيخ له وليظهر أنه معاند ولذلك لم يتب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r8.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r8.claim: Al-Zajjaj says Iblis answers the implied question of which was better, adding that superiority was what kept him from prostrating.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r8.anchor: إنما هو جواب أيكما خير ولكن المعنى منعني من السجود فضلي عليه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r9.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r9.claim: The scholars say Iblis erred by using analogy despite an explicit command, and by overlooking clay's superiority to fire.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r9.anchor: قال العلماء وقع الخطأ من إبليس حين قاس مع وجود النص وخفي عليه فضل الطين على النار

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r10.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r10.claim: Fire is volatile, inflamed, and hasty, whereas clay is calm and steady.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r10.anchor: أحدها أن من طبع النار الطيش والالتهاب والعجلة ومن طبع الطين الهدوء والرزانة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r11.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r11.claim: Clay causes growth and coming into being, while fire causes destruction and annihilation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r11.anchor: والثاني أن الطين سبب الإنبات والإيجاد والنار سبب الإعدام والإهلاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r12.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r12.claim: Clay brings things together, whereas fire separates them.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p173/r12.anchor: والثالث أن الطين سبب جمع الأشياء والنار سبب تفريقها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r1.speaker: بعض النحاة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r1.claim: Some grammarians treat the negative particle lā here as extra.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r1.anchor: قال بعض النحاة في توجيه قوله تعالى: {ما

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r2.speaker: بعض النحاة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r2.claim: Other grammarians say lā intensifies the negation, as in the poet's combining the negative particles mā and in.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم: زيدت لتأكيد الجحد، كقول الشاعر:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r3.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r3.claim: Ibn Jarīr rejects both grammatical accounts and understands manaʿaka to imply a verb such as 'compel' or 'make necessary'; Ibn Kathīr calls this strong and good.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r3.anchor: حكاهما ابن جرير (2) وردهما، واختار أن "منعك" تضمن معنى فعل آخر تقديره:

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r4.claim: Iblis's claim that a superior should not bow to an inferior is an excuse worse than the sin: he judged by material origin and opposed an explicit divine command with corrupt analogy, ignoring Adam's special honor.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r4.anchor: من العذر الذي هو أكبر من الذنب، كأنه امتنع من الطاعة لأنه لا يؤمر الفاضل بالسجود للمفضول

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r5.claim: Iblis wrongly claimed fire nobler than clay; clay is measured, patient, receptive to growth and repair, whereas fire burns, acts rashly, and moves quickly, so Adam's element helped him repent and submit while Iblis betrayed his.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r5.anchor: فإن الطين من شأنه الرزانة والحلم والأناة والتثبت، والطين محل النبات والنمو والزيادة والإصلاح.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r6.claim: The verb ablasa means that Iblis despaired of mercy after refusing to prostrate.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r6.anchor: أبلس من الرحمة، أي: أيس من الرحمة،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r7.speaker: عائشة عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r7.claim: A report in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim says the angels were created from light, Iblis from a flame of fire, and Adam from what has been described in the Qur'an.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r7.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم، عن عائشة، رضي الله عنها، قالت: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "خلقت الملائكة من نور، وخلق إبليس من مارج من نار،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r8.speaker: عائشة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r8.claim: Ibn Mardawayh transmits from ʿĀʾisha a version saying the angels were created from the light of the Throne, the jinn from a flame of fire, and Adam as described in the Qur'an.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r8.anchor: وقال ابن مردويه: حدثنا عبد الله بن جعفر، حدثنا إسماعيل، عن عبد الله بن مسعود، حدثنا نعيم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r9.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r9.claim: A wording found in some versions outside the sound collection adds that the houris were created from saffron.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p392/r9.anchor: وفي بعض ألفاظ هذا الحديث في غير الصحيح: "وخلقت الحور العين من الزعفران"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p393/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p393/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p393/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan says Iblis reasoned by analogy and was the first to do so; Ibn Jarīr's chain for this report is sound.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p393/r1.anchor: عن الحسن في قوله: {خلقتني من نار وخلقته من طين} قال: قاس إبليس، وهو أول من قاس. إسناده صحيح.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p393/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p393/r2.speaker: ابن سيرين
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p393/r2.claim: Ibn Sīrīn says Iblis was the first to reason by analogy and that the sun and moon were worshipped only through analogical reasoning; Ibn Jarīr calls the chain sound.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p393/r2.anchor: عن هشام، عن ابن سيرين قال: أول من قاس إبليس، وما عبدت الشمس والقمر إلا بالمقاييس

JISHUMI:v4p2508/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2508/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2508/r4.claim: Three analyses are offered: لا is an emphatic extra particle, the phrase means 'what prompted you not to prostrate,' or it means 'what impelled you to refuse'; al-Farra sees reinforcement after the preceding negation, and another parses it as 'who told you not to prostrate?'.
JISHUMI:v4p2508/r4.anchor: قوله: ما منعك ألا تسجد فيه ثلاثة أقوال: الأول: أن تكون (لا) صلة مؤكدة

JISHUMI:v4p2508/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2508/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2508/r5.claim: ما is nominative as 'what thing prevented you'; أن is accusative as the object of منع.
JISHUMI:v4p2508/r5.anchor: رفع على تقدير: أي شيء منعك من السجود، و(أن) في موضع نصب بوقوع المنع عليهما

JISHUMI:v4p2508/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2508/r10.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v4p2508/r10.claim: Abu ʿAli says the statement was spoken by one of the angels on God's behalf.
JISHUMI:v4p2508/r10.anchor: قاله على لسان بعض ملائكته، عن أبي علي

JISHUMI:v4p2508/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2508/r11.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v4p2508/r11.claim: Another view says God Himself spoke the words, as the miracle indicates.
JISHUMI:v4p2508/r11.anchor: وقيل: [بل قاله الله]- تعالى -[ودل المعجز] أنه كلامه

JISHUMI:v4p2508/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2508/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2508/r12.claim: The question asks what turned Iblis away, not what literally prevented him, since he was not barred from obeying an order; a diversion is like prevention, just as a summons is like compulsion.
JISHUMI:v4p2508/r12.anchor: وليس المراد المنع؛ لأنه لم يكن ممنوعا من السجود إذ لو كان ممنوعا لما أمر به

JISHUMI:v4p2508/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v4p2508/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v4p2508/r13.claim: Iblis argues that fire is superior to clay, therefore he is better than Adam and will not prostrate to him.
JISHUMI:v4p2508/r13.anchor: فلما كان النار خيرا من الطين كنت خيرا من آدم، فلا أسجد له

MUQATIL:7:10-12/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:7:10-12/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:7:10-12/r5.claim: Iblis claims superiority because he was created from fire and Adam from clay; fire overcomes clay.
MUQATIL:7:10-12/r5.anchor: { قال ما منعك ألا تسجد إذ أمرتك قال أنا خير منه خلقتنى من نار وخلقته من طين } [آية: 12]، والنار تغلب الطين

NASAFI-FULL:v2p4#7/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p4#7/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p4#7/r1.claim: The question asks what prevented Iblīs from prostrating; «lā» is extra, as in the parallel passages 38:75 and 57:29.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p4#7/r1.anchor: ولا زائدة بدليل ما منعك أن تسجد لما خلقت بيدي

NASAFI-FULL:v2p4#7/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p4#7/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p4#7/r2.claim: The construction is linked to 38:75 and 57:29, where the corresponding «lā» is also treated as extra.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p4#7/r2.anchor: بدليل ما منعك أن تسجد لما خلقت بيدي ومثلها لئلا يعلم أهل الكتاب

NASAFI-FULL:v2p4#7/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p4#7/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p4#7/r3.claim: The command shows that commands entail obligation; asking about the obstacle despite knowing it rebukes Iblīs and exposes his defiance, disbelief, and pride.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p4#7/r3.anchor: فيه دليل على أن الأمر للوجوب والسؤال عن المانع من السجود مع علمه به للتوبيخ

NASAFI-FULL:v2p4#7/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p4#7/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p4#7/r4.claim: Iblīs wrongly claimed superiority: clay has weight, patience, modesty, and endurance, while fire is impulsive, proud, destructive, and treacherous; earth fosters trust and growth.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p4#7/r4.anchor: وقد أخطأ الخبيث بل الطين أفضل لرزانته ووقاره ومنه الحلم والحياء والصبر

NASAFI-FULL:v2p4#7/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p4#7/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p4#7/r5.claim: Iblīs was the first to use analogy, but analogy is invalid against an explicit text; his comparison defied the command and relied on a false measure.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p4#7/r5.anchor: وقول نافى القياس أول من قاس ابليس قياس على أن القياس عند مثبته مردود عند وجود النص

NASAFI-FULL:v2p4#7/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p4#7/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p4#7/r6.claim: Rather than answer directly, Iblīs claimed superiority and its cause, implicitly saying that this supposed superiority stopped him; he deemed a superior prostrating to an inferior irrational.
NASAFI-FULL:v2p4#7/r6.anchor: لأنه قد استأنف قصة وأخبر فيها عن نفسه بالفضل على آدم عليه السلام وبعلة فضله عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r1.claim: Ma is a nominative subject meaning 'what thing'; the question is a rebuke.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r1.anchor: «ما» في موضع رفع بالابتداء أي أي شيء منعك. وهذا سؤال توبيخ.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r2.claim: One analysis parses alla tasjuda as accusative with an understood min, 'from prostrating,' and treats la as extra.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r2.anchor: { ألا تسجد } في موضع نصب، أي من أن تسجد. و «لا» زائدة.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r3.claim: A poem shows la can be extra: the intended meaning is that his generosity refused stinginess.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r3.anchor: أبى جوده لا البخل فاستعجلت به نعم من فتى لا يمنع الجود نائله

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r4.claim: Another analysis keeps la meaningful: prevention can involve speech or invitation, so the question is who told Iblis not to prostrate.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r4.anchor: وقيل ليست بزائدة فإن المنع فيه طرف من القول والدعاء، فكأنه قال: من قال لك ألا تسجد؟

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r5.claim: A further analysis supplies an ellipsis: what kept you from obedience and made you need not to prostrate?
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r5.anchor: وقيل: في الكلام حذف، والتقدير: ما منعك من الطاعة وأحوجك إلى ألا تسجد.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r6.claim: Arrogance and envy made Iblis refuse; he had concealed this intention when the command was announced before Adam's creation.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r6.anchor: قال العلماء: الذي أحوجه إلى ترك السجود هو الكبر والحسد: وكان أضمر ذلك في نفسه إذا أمر بذلك

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r7.claim: Prostration lowered the one prostrating while honoring the one honored; when angels fell, Iblis stayed standing and disclosed his inward refusal.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r7.anchor: فإن في الوقوع توضيع الواقع وتشريفا لمن وقع له فأضمر في نفسه ألا يسجد إذا أمره في ذلك الوقت.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r8.claim: God's question drew out Iblis's secret: what prevented him from submitting to God's command?
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r8.anchor: أي ما منعك من الانقياد لأمري فأخرج سر ضميره فقال: { أنا خير منه }

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r9.claim: The rebuke for leaving God's unqualified command supports the principle that an imperative entails obligation without a contrary indicator.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r9.anchor: يدل على ما يقوله الفقهاء من أن الأمر يقتضي الوجوب بمطلقه من غير قرينة

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r10.claim: Iblis means his supposed superiority kept him from prostrating; this is an answer in meaning rather than a literal answer.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r10.anchor: أي منعني من السجود فضلي عليه فهذا من إبليس جواب على المعنى.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r11.claim: Iblis judged fire superior because it rises, is light, and is a luminous substance.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r11.anchor: فرأى أن النار أشرف من الطين لعلوها وصعودها وخفتها، ولأنها جوهر مضيء.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan, and Ibn Sirin say Iblis was first to make an analogy and erred; Ibn Sirin says those reasoning about religion by opinion are paired with him.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r12.anchor: قال ابن عباس والحسن وابن سيرين: أول من قاس إبليس فأخطأ القياس. فمن قاس الدين برأيه قرنه الله مع إبليس.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r13.speaker: ابن سيرين
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r13.claim: Ibn Sirin says the sun and moon were worshipped only through analogical reasoning.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12/r13.anchor: قال ابن سيرين: وما عبدت الشمس والقمر إلا بالمقاييس.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r1.speaker: القفال
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r1.claim: Al-Qaffal contrasts clay's stabilizing virtues, which brought Adam to repentance and forgiveness, with fire's volatility, which drove Iblis to arrogance and ruin.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r1.anchor: وذلك هو الداعي لإبليس بعد الشقاوة التي سبقت له إلى الاستكبار والإصرار فأورثه الهلاك والعذاب واللعنة والشقاء قاله القفال.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r2.speaker: القفال
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r2.claim: Fire's lightness, rashness, sharpness, elevation, and instability led Iblis to arrogance and persistence, bringing ruin, punishment, curse, and misery.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r2.anchor: ومن جوهر النار الخفة، والطيش، والحدة، والارتفاع، والاضطراب. وذلك هو الداعي لإبليس

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r3.claim: A second argument for clay is that Paradise's soil is fragrant musk, with no report of fire in Paradise or soil in Hell.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r3.anchor: إن الخبر ناطق بأن تراب الجنة مسك أذفر، ولم ينطق الخبر بأن في الجنة نارا وأن في النار ترابا.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r4.claim: A third argument is that fire is a means of punishment and God's punishment for His enemies, while soil is not a cause of punishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r4.anchor: أن النار سبب العذاب، وهي عذاب الله لأعدائه وليس التراب سببا للعذاب.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r5.claim: A fourth argument is that clay needs no fire, while fire needs a place and its place is earth.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r5.anchor: أن الطين مستغن عن النار، والنار محتاجة إلى المكان ومكانها التراب.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r6.claim: Al-Qurtubi adds soil as a place of prayer and purification; fire warns and punishes, as 39:16 says.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r6.anchor: قلت ويحتمل قولا خامسا وهو أن التراب مسجد وطهور كما جاء في صحيح الحديث.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r7.claim: Fire is linked to warning and punishment through the verse that God frightens His servants with it.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas says obedience was more fitting for Iblis than analogy; he disobeyed God and was first to reason from his own opinion.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: كانت الطاعة أولى بإبليس من القياس فعصى ربه، وهو أول من قاس برأيه.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r9.claim: Analogy contradicting revealed text is rejected.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r10.claim: Al-Qurtubi endorses the first view: analogy is rationally permissible and legislated; Companions, Successors, and the majority accept it.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r10.anchor: فهم الصحابة والتابعون، وجمهور من بعدهم، وأن التعبد به جائز عقلا واقع شرعا، وهو الصحيح.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r11.speaker: القفال
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r11.claim: Al-Qaffal and Abu al-Husayn al-Basri hold that analogy is rationally obligatory.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r11.anchor: وذهب القفال من الشافعية وأبو الحسين البصري إلى وجوب التعبد به عقلا.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r12.speaker: النظام
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r12.claim: Al-Nazzam says analogy is impossible rationally and legally; some literalists also reject it.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r12.anchor: وذهب النظام إلى أنه يستحيل التعبد به عقلا وشرعا ورده بعض أهل الظاهر.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r13.speaker: البخاري
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r13.claim: Al-Bukhari says authority lies in scripture, Sunna, or scholarly consensus if a ruling is found there; otherwise analogy applies, with chapters on comparing known cases and evidentiary rulings.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r13.anchor: قال البخاري في كتاب الاعتصام بالكتاب والسنة: المعنى لا عصمة لأحد إلا في كتاب الله أو سنة نبيه أو في إجماع العلماء

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r14.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r14.claim: Al-Tabari calls inference from the Book, Sunna, and consensus the true, binding duty of scholars, supported by reports from the Prophet, Companions, and Successors.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r14.anchor: وقال الطبري: الإجتهاد والاستنباط من كتاب الله وسنة نبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم وإجماع الأمة هو الحق الواجب، والفرض اللازم لأهل العلم.
