QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r15.speaker: أبو تمام المالكي
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r15.claim: Abu Tammam says the community agreed on analogy, including comparing gold and silver for zakat.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r15.anchor: وقال أبو تمام المالكي: أجمعت الأمة على القياس فمن ذلك أنهم أجمعوا على قياس الذهب والورق في الزكاة.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r16.speaker: علي
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r16.claim: Ali rejects Abu Bakr's request to be released from the pledge: since the Prophet chose him for religion, they should accept him for worldly leadership; this analogizes imamate to prayer leadership.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r16.anchor: فقال علي: والله لا نقيلك ولا نستقيلك، رضيك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لديننا أفلا نرضاك لدنيانا؟

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r17.speaker: أبو بكر
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r17.claim: Abu Bakr analogized zakat to prayer, refusing to separate two things God had joined.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r17.anchor: وقاس الصديق الزكاة على الصلاة وقال: والله لا أفرق بين ما جمع الله.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r18.speaker: علي
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r18.claim: Ali analogized the drunkard's penalty to that for slander: drunkenness makes him rant and then accuse others.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r18.anchor: وصرح علي بالقياس في شارب الخمر بمحضر من الصحابة وقال: إنه إذا سكر هذى، وإذا هذى افترى

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r19.speaker: عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r19.claim: Umar tells Abu Musa to reason from scripture and Sunna, identify comparable cases, and choose the judgment closest to God's favor and justice.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#2/r19.anchor: وكتب عمر إلى أبي موسى الأشعري كتابا فيه: الفهم الفهم فيما يختلج في صدرك مما لم يبلغك في الكتاب والسنة

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#3/r1.speaker: الدارقطني
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#3/r1.claim: Al-Daraqutni transmits Umar's full report about guidance to Abu Musa on reasoning from comparable cases.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#3/r2.speaker: عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#3/r2.claim: Asked whether retreat from plague fled God's decree, Umar answered it moved from one decree to another and reasoned with Abu Ubayda before the Emigrants and Helpers.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#3/r2.anchor: وقد قال أبو عبيدة لعمر رضي الله عنهما في حديث الوباء، حين رجع عمر من سرغ: نفر من قدر الله؟ فقال عمر: نعم! نفر من قدر الله إلى قدر الله.

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#3/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#3/r3.claim: Analogy is a foundation of religion and safeguard for Muslims, used by qualified scholars to derive rulings; this is the authoritative majority position.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#3/r3.anchor: وهو يدل على أن القياس أصل من أصول الدين، وعصمة من عصم المسلمين، يرجع إليه المجتهدون

QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#3/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#3/r4.claim: Blameworthy opinion and contrived analogy lack legal foundations, amount to conjecture and satanic prompting; 17:36 forbids following what one does not know. Weak anti-analogy reports concern this baseless form.
QURTUBI-FULL:7:12#3/r4.anchor: وأما الرأي المذموم والقياس المتكلف المنهي عنه فهو ما لم يكن على هذه الأصول المذكورة لأن ذلك ظن ونزغ من الشيطان

BURSEVI:v3p106#4/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p106#4/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p106#4/r1.claim: ألا means أن تسجد, with لا treated as extra, as in 57:29, where لئلا conveys that the People of the Book may know.
BURSEVI:v3p106#4/r1.anchor: أي : أن تسجدو لا صلة كما في قوله تعالى

BURSEVI:v3p106#4/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p106#4/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p106#4/r2.claim: The command refers to the time God ordered Iblis to prostrate.
BURSEVI:v3p106#4/r2.anchor: إذ أمرتك} أي : وقت أمري إياك به

BURSEVI:v3p106#4/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p106#4/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p106#4/r3.claim: Iblis claimed superiority because fire is subtle and luminous while clay is dense and dark; the author says he erred by judging virtue from material and element.
BURSEVI:v3p106#4/r3.anchor: والنار جوهر لطيف نوراني ، والطين جسم كثيف ظلماني

BURSEVI:v3p106#4/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p106#4/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p106#4/r4.claim: The Persian verses contrast Adam's outward form with divine light, warning against judging by appearance while ignoring spiritual meaning.
BURSEVI:v3p106#4/r4.anchor: زآدمي إبليس صورت ديد وبس غافل ازمعنى شد آن مردود خس

BURSEVI:v3p106#4/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p106#4/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p106#4/r5.claim: The Masnavi has fire claim superiority over clay, but God's answer makes piety the measure of merit, not lineage.
BURSEVI:v3p106#4/r5.anchor: كفت نار ازخاك بي شك بهترست

BURSEVI:v3p106#4/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p106#4/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v3p106#4/r6.claim: Adam's honor and virtue over the angels were not simply due to properties of clay or to being kneaded without an intermediary.
BURSEVI:v3p106#4/r6.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : أن شرف مسجودية آدم وفضيلته على ساجديه

BURSEVI:v3p106#4/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v3p106#4/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v3p106#4/r7.claim: The poem warns against relying on analogy when the sun of certainty or Kaaba is present, urging submission to God's superior knowledge.
BURSEVI:v3p106#4/r7.anchor: ليك با خورشيد وكعبه يش رو اين قياس واين تحرى را مجو

RAZI-FULL:v14p27#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p27#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p27#2/r1.claim: The command to prostrate included Iblis, apparently implying he was an angel, although Razi says the earlier proofs establish otherwise and the exception was addressed under al-Baqara.
RAZI-FULL:v14p27#2/r1.anchor: فإن ذلك الأمر قد تناول إبليس

RAZI-FULL:v14p27#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p27#2/r2.speaker: الكسائي والفراء والزجاج والأكثرون
RAZI-FULL:v14p27#2/r2.claim: The popular grammatical view treats la as extra, yielding “What prevented you from prostrating?”; al-Kisaʾi, al-Farraʾ, al-Zajjaj, and most scholars hold this.
RAZI-FULL:v14p27#2/r2.anchor: وهذا قول الكسائي ، والفراء ، والزجاج ، والأكثرين

RAZI-FULL:v14p27#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p27#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p27#2/r3.claim: Razi prefers that la carries meaning, since declaring a word in God’s Book useless is difficult and problematic.
RAZI-FULL:v14p27#2/r3.anchor: ههنا مفيدة وليست لغوا وهذا هو الصحيح

RAZI-FULL:v14p27#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p27#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p27#2/r4.claim: One meaningful reading asks what stopped Iblis from refraining from prostration, as an accusatory rhetorical question implying that no such restraint existed.
RAZI-FULL:v14p27#2/r4.anchor: ويكون هذا الاستفهام على سبيل الإنكار

RAZI-FULL:v14p27#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p27#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p27#2/r5.claim: The analogy is a question to someone who unjustly struck the speaker: what prevented him—religion, reason, or shame?—implying none did.
RAZI-FULL:v14p27#2/r5.anchor: كقول القائل لمن ضربه ظلما : ما

RAZI-FULL:v14p27#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p27#2/r6.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v14p27#2/r6.claim: Al-Qadi reads “prevented” as “prompted”: God asks what induced Iblis not to prostrate, since defying God’s command is astonishing.
RAZI-FULL:v14p27#2/r6.anchor: قال القاضي : ذكر الله المنع وأراد الداعي

RAZI-FULL:v14p27#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p27#2/r7.speaker: العلماء
RAZI-FULL:v14p27#2/r7.claim: Scholars infer that a command form entails obligation because God blamed Iblis for leaving what He had commanded.
RAZI-FULL:v14p27#2/r7.anchor: احتج العلماء بهذه الآية على أن صيغة الأمر تفيد الوجوب

RAZI-FULL:v14p28/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p28/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p28/r1.claim: The phrase “when I commanded you” explains the blame by the command simply as a command, not a special instance; therefore every command entails obligation.
RAZI-FULL:v14p28/r1.anchor: هو الأمر من حيث أنه أمر لا كونه أمرا مخصوصا

RAZI-FULL:v14p28/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p28/r2.speaker: المحتجون بأن الأمر يفيد الفور
RAZI-FULL:v14p28/r2.claim: Those who say commands require immediate performance argue that Iblis was blamed for failing to prostrate at once; otherwise immediate delay would not warrant blame.
RAZI-FULL:v14p28/r2.anchor: ذم إبليس على ترك السجود في الحال

RAZI-FULL:v14p28#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p28#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p28#2/r1.claim: Iblis says he refused because he considered himself superior and believed a superior being should not be ordered to serve an inferior; fire, he argues, is better than clay.
RAZI-FULL:v14p28#2/r1.anchor: ومن كان خيرا من غيره فإنه لا يجوز أمر ذلك الأكمل بالسجود لذلك الأدون

RAZI-FULL:v14p28#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p28#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p28#2/r2.claim: Iblis’s case ranks fire above clay as celestial, subtle, light, and active, while clay is dark, low, dense, heavy, and receptive; it associates fire with life and earthiness with death.
RAZI-FULL:v14p28#2/r2.anchor: والأرض ليس لها إلا القبول والانفعال . والفعل أشرف من الانفعال

RAZI-FULL:v14p28#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p28#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p28#2/r3.claim: He also appeals to heat’s role in ripening fruit and growth, contrasting it with cold, dry old age, which he calls the worst period of human life.

RAZI-FULL:v14p28#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p28#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p28#2/r4.claim: Razi rejects the premise that superior material makes a superior form: virtue is a gift from God, so a better origin does not guarantee a better creature.
RAZI-FULL:v14p28#2/r4.anchor: لما كانت الفضيلة عطية من الله ابتداء لم يلزم من فضيلة المادة فضيلة الصورة

RAZI-FULL:v14p28#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p28#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p28#2/r5.claim: God brings a disbeliever from a believer and a believer from a disbeliever, and light from darkness and vice versa; virtue therefore comes from God, not the original substance.
RAZI-FULL:v14p28#2/r5.anchor: وذلك يدل على أن الفضيلة لا تحصل إلا بفضل الله تعالى لا بسبب فضيلة الأصل والجوهر

RAZI-FULL:v14p28#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p28#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p28#2/r6.claim: Moral responsibility concerns the living person after reaching mature reason, so evaluation depends on what the person becomes, not the material from which he was made.
RAZI-FULL:v14p28#2/r6.anchor: فالمعتبر بما انتهى إليه لا بما خلق منه

RAZI-FULL:v14p28#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p28#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p28#2/r7.claim: Merit comes from deeds rather than material origin: a believing Abyssinian is better than an unbelieving Qurayshi.
RAZI-FULL:v14p28#2/r7.anchor: وأيضا فالفضل إنما يكون بالأعمال وما يتصل بها

RAZI-FULL:v14p28#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p28#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p28#2/r8.claim: Iblis’s further premise is that it is rationally indecent to command a superior to serve an inferior; Razi illustrates it with leading jurists ordered to serve a lesser jurist.
RAZI-FULL:v14p28#2/r8.anchor: أن من أمر أبا حنيفة والشافعي وسائر أكابر الفقهاء بخدمة فقيه نازل الدرجة كان ذلك قبيحا في العقول

RAZI-FULL:v14p29/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p29/r1.speaker: المحتجون بمنع تخصيص العموم بالقياس
RAZI-FULL:v14p29/r1.claim: Opponents of specifying general scripture by analogy argue that the general command included Iblis, who exempted himself through a fire-over-clay analogy; his severe blame shows such specification is impermissible.
RAZI-FULL:v14p29/r1.anchor: احتج من قال : أنه لا يجوز تخصيص عموم النص بالقياس

RAZI-FULL:v14p29/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p29/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v14p29/r4.claim: Al-Wahidi reports Ibn Abbas saying obedience was preferable to analogy for Iblis: he disobeyed and analogized, became the first to analogize and disbelieved, and God joins self-directed religious analogizers with him.
RAZI-FULL:v14p29/r4.anchor: ابن عباس أنه قال : كانت الطاعة أولى بإبليس من القياس

RAZI-FULL:v14p29#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p29#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p29#2/r4.claim: God asks why Iblis did not prostrate; Iblis answers that he was made from fire and Adam from clay; God then orders Iblis to descend.
RAZI-FULL:v14p29#2/r4.anchor: لا شك أن قائل هذا القول هو الله

RAZI-FULL:v14p30/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p30/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v14p30/r1.claim: Razi asks why Iblis received direct divine speech if such speech honors Moses; if it does not confer honor, why does scripture present God’s speech to Moses as a great distinction?
RAZI-FULL:v14p30/r1.anchor: فإن كانت هذه المكالمة تفيد الشرف العظيم فكيف حصلت على أعظم الوجوه لإبليس

RAZI-FULL:v14p30/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v14p30/r2.speaker: بعض العلماء
RAZI-FULL:v14p30/r2.claim: Some scholars say God addressed Iblis through an angelic intermediary, since they hold that God speaks to non-prophets only through a mediator.
RAZI-FULL:v14p30/r2.anchor: أن بعض العلماء قال : إنه تعالى قال لإبليس
